papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Unifying Tool: Beyond Compression to Privacy, Robustness, Fairness, and Theory
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation began as a technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, faster models, but its utility now spans privacy-preserving training, robustness transfer, fairness mitigation, domain generalization, and theoretical insights about learning. Distillation can (1) produce compact models that retain most of a teacher's performance, (2) transfer nontrivial inductive biases and robustness properties, and (3) be adapted to settings with privacy constraints or imperfect teachers. However, distillation is not a panacea: teacher errors, choice of distilled data, and sample-level effects can harm the student unless carefully managed. This perspective synthesizes empirical and theoretical evidence to argue that knowledge distillation is a central, flexible methodology for modern deep learning, while highlighting practical constraints and directions for responsible application.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Trade-offs, and Empirical Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques seek to transfer predictive power and internal knowledge from large, expensive models (teachers) into smaller, faster models (students), enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Approaches vary from matching teacher output distributions to transferring intermediate representations, designing many-to-many layer mappings, performing data-free distillation when original training data are unavailable, and distilling ensembles or multiple teachers into a single model. In NLP, these methods are applied to compress pre-trained language models, speed up evaluation metrics, and produce task-adaptive compressed models while attempting to retain generalization and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques are widely used to transfer behavior from large teacher models to smaller students, enabling deployment under resource constraints. Research over the past decade has developed variants that target outputs (soft labels), internal representations (layer-wise and attention-based methods), data regimes (data-free or distilled training sets), and architecture search for task-aware compression. Empirical and theoretical work highlights both the practical gains and fundamental limits of distillation, and points to best practices such as pre-training compact models, selecting or synthesizing appropriate training data, and aligning student capacity to distilled signal.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and adaptable family of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster models suitable for deployment. Beyond the classic teacher-logit supervision, modern distillation covers feature-level matching, task-adaptive architecture search, multi-teacher transfer, and data-free scenarios. KD can be combined with pruning and structured sparsity, adapted for domain shifts, and used to transfer ensemble or task-specific knowledge into compact models. The choice of distillation target, the availability of data, and the deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy, domain) determine which distillation recipe will be most effective.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile model-compression paradigm that transfers predictive behavior from larger (teacher) models to smaller (student) models. Work across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks has expanded KD beyond soft-label matching to include internal representation matching, layer mapping, feature attention, curriculum strategies, data-side techniques (including data-free methods and augmentation-aware KD), multi-teacher weighting, and task-specific adaptations. Empirical and theoretical analyses show that KD can act both as a conduit of teacher “dark knowledge” (similarity structure among classes) and as a regularizer related to label smoothing; practical improvements require matching the right kinds of knowledge (outputs, intermediate features, relational signals) and addressing mismatches in inputs, data distributions, and training curricula. Applications in NLP (e.g., retrieval, translation, spoken QA) illustrate how KD strategies must be adapted to task structure and data idiosyncrasies to preserve quality on low-frequency phenomena while achieving significant runtime and memory savings.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Curriculum Learning for Dense Retrieval Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent work has shown that more effective dense retrieval models can be obtained by distilling ranking knowledge from an existing base re-ranking model. In this paper, we propose a generic curriculum learning based optimization framework called CL-DRD that controls the difficulty level of training data produced by the re-ranking (teacher) model. CL-DRD iteratively optimizes the dense retrieval (student) model by increasing the difficulty of the knowledge distillation data made available to it. In more detail, we initially provide the student model coarse-grained preference pairs between documents in the teacher's ranking and progressively move towards finer-grained pairwise document ordering requirements. In our experiments, we apply a simple implementation of the CL-DRD framework to enhance two state-of-the-art dense retrieval models. Experiments on three public passage retrieval datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework.

papers_seen.author: Nunez
papers_seen.title: Beyond Compression: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Tool for Practical, Private, and Robust Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is often framed narrowly as a model-compression trick to shrink large neural networks. This paper argues KD should instead be viewed as a core engineering and scientific tool for practical deployment: it enables training with limited or private data, yields task- and domain-adaptive compact models, improves robustness and fairness, and transfers intermediate representations and attention patterns that standard supervised training cannot. We synthesize evidence from recent work to show how variants of KD—self-distillation, layer-wise projection, multi-teacher schemes, teacher annealing, and data-free distillation—address concrete deployment challenges in vision and NLP, and we derive practical recommendations for combining these techniques in real systems.

papers_seen.author: Estes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Toolbox: Principles, Limits, and Practical Prescriptions for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation should be understood and applied as a flexible set of techniques that go well beyond simple parameter compression. When treated as a toolbox—combining soft-target supervision, internal representation matching, layer-aware alignment, attention-guided mapping, and complementary compression methods—distillation can produce compact models that preserve accuracy, improve interpretability, and transfer robustness or privacy properties. Success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to prepare the student, and how to mitigate propagation of teacher defects; practitioners benefit from system-level designs that pair distillation objectives with pre-training, data augmentation, and architecture-aware compression.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Lambert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring aspects of teacher behavior. The field has expanded from soft-label (logit) supervision to diverse strategies including feature- and representation-level imitation, flexible layer mapping, online/co-distillation, data- and domain-aware augmentation, and multimodal-to-mono-modal transfer. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost, but success depends on what is transferred (soft targets, features, relations), how teacher and student architectures are aligned, the availability and quality of distillation data, and deployment constraints such as privacy, domain shift, and compute budget. Open challenges include selecting the right distillation targets for task and capacity gap, ensuring robustness and fairness post-compression, and automating adaptive distillation pipelines for heterogeneous production settings.

papers_seen.author: Spears
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble models into smaller students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure. It is a practical toolkit used to reduce memory, compute, and latency for deployment, to enable low-precision inference, to adapt models across domains, and to support privacy-aware or federated settings. Empirical work across vision, speech, graphs, and language tasks shows that careful choices about what to transfer, how teachers are configured, and how training is regularized materially affect the trade-offs between efficiency and task performance.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Channel Distillation: Channel-Wise Attention for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is to transfer the knowledge from the data learned by the teacher network to the student network, so that the student has the advantage of less parameters and less calculations, and the accuracy is close to the teacher. In this paper, we propose a new distillation method, which contains two transfer distillation strategies and a loss decay strategy. The first transfer strategy is based on channel-wise attention, called Channel Distillation (CD). CD transfers the channel information from the teacher to the student. The second is Guided Knowledge Distillation (GKD). Unlike Knowledge Distillation (KD), which allows the student to mimic each sample's prediction distribution of the teacher, GKD only enables the student to mimic the correct output of the teacher. The last part is Early Decay Teacher (EDT). During the training process, we gradually decay the weight of the distillation loss. The purpose is to enable the student to gradually control the optimization rather than the teacher. Our proposed method is evaluated on ImageNet and CIFAR100. On ImageNet, we achieve 27.68% of top-1 error with ResNet18, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On CIFAR100, we achieve surprising result that the student outperforms the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/zhouzaida/channel-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Complementarities
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques enable deployment of large deep models by transferring knowledge from high-capacity teachers to smaller students or by combining compression methods. Work in this area spans practical recipe development for NLP and vision models, theoretical analyses of when and why distillation helps, methods that go beyond soft logits to internal feature transfer, strategies for multi-teacher and ensemble compression, approaches for data-limited or data-free settings, and complementary compression techniques such as pruning and quantization. Empirical results show that careful choices (e.g., which samples or layers to use, how to combine teachers, and how to map teacher-to-student layers) matter for final accuracy; theoretical results explain tradeoffs between soft and hard labels, and methods exist that make distillation feasible without teacher data or with constrained hardware.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Variants, and Practical Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring aspects of the teacher’s predictive behavior and internal representations. A diverse set of methods—matching output distributions, aligning intermediate features, progressive module replacement, multi-teacher and data-free schemes, and task- or domain-aware adaptations—has been developed to address deployment constraints such as latency, memory, data availability, privacy, and multimodal inputs. Empirical work shows that when the distillation recipe is matched to model architectures, data conditions, and deployment constraints, students can retain much of the teacher’s performance while offering practical efficiency gains; however, trade-offs and open challenges remain around robustness, domain shift, and faithful transfer of rare or fine-grained behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: MixKD: Towards Efficient Distillation of Large-scale Language Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale language models have recently demonstrated impressive empirical performance. Nevertheless, the improved results are attained at the price of bigger models, more power consumption, and slower inference, which hinder their applicability to low-resource (both memory and computation) platforms. Knowledge distillation (KD) has been demonstrated as an effective framework for compressing such big models. However, large-scale neural network systems are prone to memorize training instances, and thus tend to make inconsistent predictions when the data distribution is altered slightly. Moreover, the student model has few opportunities to request useful information from the teacher model when there is limited task-specific data available. To address these issues, we propose MixKD, a data-agnostic distillation framework that leverages mixup, a simple yet efficient data augmentation approach, to endow the resulting model with stronger generalization ability. Concretely, in addition to the original training examples, the student model is encouraged to mimic the teacher's behavior on the linear interpolation of example pairs as well. We prove from a theoretical perspective that under reasonable conditions MixKD gives rise to a smaller gap between the generalization error and the empirical error. To verify its effectiveness, we conduct experiments on the GLUE benchmark, where MixKD consistently leads to significant gains over the standard KD training, and outperforms several competitive baselines. Experiments under a limited-data setting and ablation studies further demonstrate the advantages of the proposed approach.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach to convert large, accurate models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—choosing what teacher signals to transfer, aligning mismatched architectures, and addressing data constraints—KD can preserve most teacher performance while enabling orders-of-magnitude improvements in latency, memory footprint, and deployability. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on representations transferred, the provenance and augmentation of distillation data, and deployment constraints such as privacy or distributed training. Effective compression therefore treats KD as a core tool within a broader toolkit that includes feature-level alignment, data-aware strategies, online or multi-teacher setups, and data-free techniques when real data are unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Knowledge Distillation in NLP: Pre-training, Task-Awareness, Privacy, and Robustness
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large language models into smaller, faster students for NLP applications. Its effectiveness depends not only on the student-teacher framework but on complementary practices: pre-training compact models, aligning distilled signals to task-relevant representations, handling limited or private data, leveraging multiple teachers when available, and explicitly distilling for robustness. When these elements are combined and tuned, distillation yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Cornerstone of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. KD operates at multiple levels (soft targets, intermediate representations, relational structure) and can be combined with complementary compression techniques and data strategies to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When tailored to model architecture, task demands, and available data, KD yields compact models that enable real-world deployment across modalities and domains.

papers_seen.author: Ware
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical System for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential and practical approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a system—covering teacher design, the training signal, data and augmentation, and efficiency constraints—KD can retain much of a teacher's performance while meeting latency, memory, and domain requirements. However, its success depends on careful choices about teacher quality, distillation objectives, available data, and complementary compression techniques; awareness of these factors yields the most reliable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Efficient Transformer-based Large Scale Language Representations using Hardware-friendly Block Structured Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. Experimental results on different models (BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT) on the General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE) benchmark tasks show that we achieve up to 5.0x with zero or minor accuracy degradation on certain task(s). Our proposed method is also orthogonal to existing compact pre-trained language models such as DistilBERT using knowledge distillation, since a further 1.79x average compression rate can be achieved on top of DistilBERT with zero or minor accuracy degradation. It is suitable to deploy the final compressed model on resource-constrained edge devices.

papers_seen.author: House
papers_seen.title: Practical Knowledge Distillation for Deploying Large NLP and Deep Models: A Unified Argument for Multi-Teacher, Data-Agnostic, and Federated Techniques
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and essential set of techniques for compressing large deep and language models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, privacy, and device-heterogeneity constraints. A mature KD strategy must simultaneously preserve teacher knowledge, generalize across domains and distributions, and respect deployment constraints (e.g., lack of original data or heterogeneous client devices). Empirical and methodological advances show that combining multi-teacher strategies, data-agnostic/distillation-from-generator approaches, feature-level projectors or ensembles, targeted augmentation, and adaptations for federated settings yields robust, efficient student models that approach teacher performance while meeting real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Improving Neural Topic Models using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Topic models are often used to identify human-interpretable topics to help make sense of large document collections. We use knowledge distillation to combine the best attributes of probabilistic topic models and pretrained transformers. Our modular method can be straightforwardly applied with any neural topic model to improve topic quality, which we demonstrate using two models having disparate architectures, obtaining state-of-the-art topic coherence. We show that our adaptable framework not only improves performance in the aggregate over all estimated topics, as is commonly reported, but also in head-to-head comparisons of aligned topics.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and widely applicable paradigm for compressing large models and transferring knowledge across architectures, tasks, and deployment constraints. A range of KD variants—data-free, federated, multi-teacher, meta-learned teachers, intermediate-feature transfer, and architecture-aware compression—have been developed to address realistic constraints such as data privacy, limited communication, teacher imperfection, and task-specific efficiency. By matching the KD strategy to the deployment constraint (e.g., privacy, compute budget, domain shift, or paucity of data) practitioners can obtain compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency and resource requirements.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: The Practical Power and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a broadly applicable and practical approach to compressing large models into smaller, faster, and—in many cases—more deployable models. When combined with complementary techniques (pre-training of compact architectures, pruning, low-precision numerics, or data-free synthesis), distillation can retain much of a teacher model's performance while meeting latency, memory, or privacy constraints. However, the success of distillation is conditional on choices about teacher-student design, access to data or surrogates, and optimization strategies; awareness of these factors yields the most reliable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Hancock
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a single recipe for copying teacher logits into a central, flexible paradigm for producing compact models that retain much of the performance and behaviors of larger teachers. KD methods vary in what they transfer (soft labels, intermediate features, relational structure), how they handle data availability (data-rich, data-free, federated), and how they combine with other compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical deployments select and tune KD components to match modality, data-privacy constraints, and latency or memory budgets.

Work across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks has expanded KD beyond soft-label matching to include internal representation matching, layer mapping, feature attention, curriculum strategies, data-side techniques (including data-free methods and augmentation-aware KD), multi-teacher weighting, and task-specific adaptations. Applications in NLP (e.g., retrieval, translation, spoken QA) illustrate how KD strategies must be adapted to task structure and data idiosyncrasies to preserve quality on low-frequency phenomena while achieving significant runtime and memory savings.'}, {'author': 'Parsons', 'year': 2018, 'title': 'Curriculum Learning for Dense Retrieval Distillation', 'abstract': "Recent work has shown that more effective dense retrieval models can be obtained by distilling ranking knowledge from an existing base re-ranking model. papers_seen.author: Duncan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, faster models by transferring information from a teacher to a student. Techniques range from matching output distributions to transferring intermediate representations, feature maps, or distilled data. Applications span model compression for deployment (including transformer compression for NLP), multimodal model adaptation, federated and resource-constrained learning, and improving robustness or fairness. Practical strategies include layer-wise or attention-based projection, progressive module replacement, adversarial and data-free distillation, and task-specific adaptations that account for data heterogeneity and inductive bias.

papers_seen.author: Patterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical, and Evolving Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a core engineering and research paradigm for compressing large models into efficient students while preserving accuracy and desirable behaviors. KD encompasses soft-target transfer, intermediate representation alignment, ensemble-to-single compression, and complementary data- and architecture-aware techniques. When treated as a design problem—choosing which signals to transfer, how to align representations, and how to manage data constraints—KD enables deployment across resource-limited and domain-shifted settings, but open challenges remain in preserving rare-token behaviors, coping with imperfect teachers, and operating without original data.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: BERT-EMD: Many-to-Many Layer Mapping for BERT Compression with Earth Mover's Distance
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) have achieved significant success in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, high storage and computational costs obstruct pre-trained language models to be effectively deployed on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose a novel BERT distillation method based on many-to-many layer mapping, which allows each intermediate student layer to learn from any intermediate teacher layers. In this way, our model can learn from different teacher layers adaptively for various NLP tasks. %motivated by the intuition that different NLP tasks require different levels of linguistic knowledge contained in the intermediate layers of BERT. In addition, we leverage Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to compute the minimum cumulative cost that must be paid to transform knowledge from teacher network to student network. EMD enables the effective matching for many-to-many layer mapping. %EMD can be applied to network layers with different sizes and effectively measures semantic distance between the teacher network and student network. Furthermore, we propose a cost attention mechanism to learn the layer weights used in EMD automatically, which is supposed to further improve the model's performance and accelerate convergence time. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Trade-offs, and Empirical Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques seek to transfer predictive power and internal knowledge from large, expensive models (teachers) into smaller, faster models (students), enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Approaches vary from matching teacher output distributions to transferring intermediate representations, designing many-to-many layer mappings, performing data-free distillation when original training data are unavailable, and distilling ensembles or multiple teachers into a single model. In NLP, these methods are applied to compress pre-trained language models, speed up evaluation metrics, and produce task-adaptive compressed models while attempting to retain generalization and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Practical Prescriptions for Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, efficient students suitable for deployment. While KD reliably reduces model size and inference cost, its effectiveness depends critically on choices around teacher design, the training signal (soft labels vs. representations), the data used for distillation, and additional constraints such as fairness and privacy. To realize reliable, high-quality compressed models in NLP and related domains, practitioners should treat KD as a system composed of complementary ingredients—data augmentation, multi-teacher or meta-learned teachers, representation-level objectives, and interventions for bias and privacy—rather than a single off-the-shelf loss.

papers_seen.author: Galloway
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Tool for Compression, Adaptation, and Robust Deployment in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central technique for transferring capabilities from large or multi-modal models into smaller, faster, or modality-limited models. When combined with complementary strategies—domain adaptation, feature-level matching, data augmentation, and meta-learning—distillation enables practical deployment across constrained devices, heterogeneous federated systems, and domain-shifted settings. However, KD is not a panacea: optimization subtleties and mismatches between teacher and student require methodological care and, in some cases, alternative regularization strategies.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Practical Strengths and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach to compress large or expensive models into smaller, faster models while retaining much of their predictive power. Across vision, speech, ranking, and natural language processing, KD enables deployment of lightweight architectures by transferring dark knowledge, feature-level signals, or ensemble behavior from teacher models. However, distillation success depends on a set of interacting choices—teacher preparation, student architecture, which signals are transferred, data and augmentation strategies, and optimization—so KD is a powerful tool when combined with careful design but not an automatic solution for all compression needs. This paper synthesizes empirical lessons and provides actionable recommendations for applying KD effectively in practice.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of large teachers. KD enables deployment under latency, storage, and privacy constraints by transferring predictive behavior and richer internal signals from teacher to student. When treated as a configurable toolkit — choosing which teacher signals to transfer, how to align representations, and which complementary compression methods to apply — distillation yields efficient models that are practical for real-world NLP and vision deployments.

papers_seen.author: Moran
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a core technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient students suitable for deployment. Across modalities and tasks, KD enables substantial reductions in memory, compute, and latency while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Success depends on choosing appropriate distillation strategies that account for model structure, task specificity, data availability, and training dynamics. When tailored—via structural transformations, progressive module replacement, task-aware layer alignment, or data-centric augmentations—distillation consistently produces compact models that approach teacher accuracy and enable real-world use cases that would otherwise be impractical.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Kidd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical, Task-Aware, and Privacy-Conscious Agenda
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical suite of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster models suitable for deployment across modalities and tasks. Effective KD goes beyond naive logits matching: task-aware layer-wise alignment, progressive module replacement, multi-teacher schedules, and architecture-aware search can preserve accuracy while reducing compute and memory. Moreover, self-distillation and teacher-free variants reduce dependence on strong teachers, and specialized KD variants address scarce data, privacy, and federated constraints. These directions together form a roadmap for applying KD in real-world deep learning and NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Understanding and Improving Lexical Choice in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is essential for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models by reducing the complexity of the raw data with an autoregressive teacher model. In this study, we empirically show that as a side effect of this training, the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words are propagated to the NAT model from the teacher model. To alleviate this problem, we propose to expose the raw data to NAT models to restore the useful information of low-frequency words, which are missed in the distilled data. To this end, we introduce an extra Kullback-Leibler divergence term derived by comparing the lexical choice of NAT model and that embedded in the raw data. Experimental results across language pairs and model architectures demonstrate the effectiveness and universality of the proposed approach. Extensive analyses confirm our claim that our approach improves performance by reducing the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach pushes the SOTA NAT performance on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets up to 27.8 and 33.8 BLEU points, respectively. The source code will be released.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Learning Compact Metrics for MT
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in machine translation and multilingual text generation have led researchers to adopt trained metrics such as COMET or BLEURT, which treat evaluation as a regression problem and use representations from multilingual pre-trained models such as XLM-RoBERTa or mBERT. Yet studies on related tasks suggest that these models are most efficient when they are large, which is costly and impractical for evaluation. We investigate the trade-off between multilinguality and model capacity with RemBERT, a state-of-the-art multilingual language model, using data from the WMT Metrics Shared Task. We present a series of experiments which show that model size is indeed a bottleneck for cross-lingual transfer, then demonstrate how distillation can help addressing this bottleneck, by leveraging synthetic data generation and transferring knowledge from one teacher to multiple students trained on related languages. Our method yields up to 10.5% improvement over vanilla fine-tuning and reaches 92.6% of RemBERT's performance using only a third of its parameters.

papers_seen.author: Whitehead
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques compress large, high-performing models into smaller, faster, or lower-precision models while retaining much of their performance. Approaches range from matching teacher soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations and using contrastive or projection-based objectives. Practical training choices—such as which layers or features to mimic, how to filter or weight training samples, the role of data augmentation, and whether compact models are pre-trained—strongly affect outcomes. KD has been applied across domains (vision, language, graphs), combined with quantization and low-precision deployment, and adapted for resource-heterogeneous and latency-sensitive settings. Empirical and theoretical work highlights that KD works both by transferring relational/representational knowledge and by providing regularizing soft targets; effective distillation designs balance these mechanisms and tailor the transfer to task and capacity constraints.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer via Adversarial Belief Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Performing knowledge transfer from a large teacher network to a smaller student is a popular task in modern deep learning applications. However, due to growing dataset sizes and stricter privacy regulations, it is increasingly common not to have access to the data that was used to train the teacher. We propose a novel method which trains a student to match the predictions of its teacher without using any data or metadata. We achieve this by training an adversarial generator to search for images on which the student poorly matches the teacher, and then using them to train the student. Our resulting student closely approximates its teacher for simple datasets like SVHN, and on CIFAR10 we improve on the state-of-the-art for few-shot distillation (with 100 images per class), despite using no data. Finally, we also propose a metric to quantify the degree of belief matching between teacher and student in the vicinity of decision boundaries, and observe a significantly higher match between our zero-shot student and the teacher, than between a student distilled with real data and the teacher. Code available at: https://github.com/polo5/ZeroShotKnowledgeTransfer

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: The Practical Centrality and Limitations of Knowledge Distillation for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a primary tool for compressing large deep models into compact, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. KD has been applied across modalities and use-cases—distilling large language models into lightweight encoders, compressing ensembles into single predictors, enabling privacy- and device-aware deployments, and even operating without access to original training data. At the same time, theoretical gaps, data- and heterogeneity-driven failure modes, and teacher biases motivate hybrid strategies (multi-teacher, meta-learned teachers, data-free generators, and combined compression techniques) to realize KD’s full potential in practical systems.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression strategies have become central tools to deploy large deep models in resource-constrained settings. The literature shows diverse KD objectives (soft-label matching, representation matching, relational/correlation losses), architectural strategies (layer-wise, task-adaptive, student-friendly teacher training), data approaches (data augmentation, distilled or synthesized surrogates, zero-shot), and multi-teacher or ensemble-to-single compression. Empirical work across vision, generative models, reinforcement learning, and language tasks (including BERT compression and non-autoregressive translation) reveals consistent trade-offs between compression, accuracy, and robustness, and highlights practical constraints such as data heterogeneity and teacher-student capacity mismatch. Below we synthesize methods, observed benefits, limitations, and practical recommendations grounded in the provided literature.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Unifying Tool: Beyond Compression to Privacy, Robustness, Fairness, and Theory
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation began as a technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, faster models, but its utility now spans privacy-preserving training, robustness transfer, fairness mitigation, domain generalization, and theoretical insights about learning. Distillation can (1) produce compact models that retain most of a teacher's performance, (2) transfer nontrivial inductive biases and robustness properties, and (3) be adapted to settings with privacy constraints or imperfect teachers. However, distillation is not a panacea: teacher errors, choice of distilled data, and sample-level effects can harm the student unless carefully managed. This perspective synthesizes empirical and theoretical evidence to argue that knowledge distillation is a central, flexible methodology for modern deep learning, while highlighting practical constraints and directions for responsible application.

papers_seen.author: Conner
papers_seen.title: Distilling Task-Specific Knowledge from BERT into Simple Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: In the natural language processing literature, neural networks are becoming increasingly deeper and complex. The recent poster child of this trend is the deep language representation model, which includes BERT, ELMo, and GPT. These developments have led to the conviction that previous-generation, shallower neural networks for language understanding are obsolete. In this paper, however, we demonstrate that rudimentary, lightweight neural networks can still be made competitive without architecture changes, external training data, or additional input features. We propose to distill knowledge from BERT, a state-of-the-art language representation model, into a single-layer BiLSTM, as well as its siamese counterpart for sentence-pair tasks. Across multiple datasets in paraphrasing, natural language inference, and sentiment classification, we achieve comparable results with ELMo, while using roughly 100 times fewer parameters and 15 times less inference time.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Powerful, Flexible — but Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods have matured into a practical toolkit for producing smaller, faster models while retaining much of the performance of larger teachers. These techniques have been applied across domains (vision, speech, NLP, healthcare), settings (offline compression, federated learning, continual adaptation), and architectures (ensembles, transformers, detectors, GANs). However, their success depends on factors such as the availability and nature of data used for distillation, domain mismatch between teacher and student, robustness and privacy requirements, and optimization dynamics. KD can unlock high-performing compact models when combined with task-aware design choices (e.g., feature imitation, augmentations, architecture search, or ensemble teachers), but practitioners must account for trade-offs and failure modes to use it effectively.

papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring useful predictive behavior and representations from a teacher to a student. Methods span matching teacher output distributions (soft labels), aligning intermediate representations or attention maps, adversarial or data-free approaches, and online or federated variants that trade communication and privacy constraints against fidelity. Practical success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to manage imperfect or heterogeneous data and devices, and whether to combine distillation with complementary compression strategies (e.g., pruning or architecture search). While distilled students often retain much of a teacher's performance and enable deployment under latency or resource constraints, open challenges include preserving rare-token behaviors, handling domain shift and robustness, and designing privacy- and communication-efficient protocols for real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Knowledge Distillation in NLP: Pre-training, Task-Awareness, Privacy, and Robustness
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large language models into smaller, faster students for NLP applications. Its effectiveness depends not only on the student-teacher framework but on complementary practices: pre-training compact models, aligning distilled signals to task-relevant representations, handling limited or private data, leveraging multiple teachers when available, and explicitly distilling for robustness. When these elements are combined and tuned, distillation yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Cornerstone of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. KD operates at multiple levels (soft targets, intermediate representations, relational structure) and can be combined with complementary compression techniques and data strategies to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When tailored to model architecture, task demands, and available data, KD yields compact models that enable real-world deployment across modalities and domains.

papers_seen.author: Cherry
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural relationships. Across vision and NLP, effective distillation combines choices about what to transfer (soft outputs, features, relational signals), how teachers are designed or ensembled, and what data or surrogates are used. Practical pipelines increasingly pair distillation with architecture search, curriculum strategies, and distributed training to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. While distillation often recovers much of a teacher's performance, success depends on careful alignment of objectives, data complexity, and optimization procedures; open problems include principled handling of imperfect teachers, robustness and fairness under compression, and scalable privacy-preserving distillation.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile technique that enables compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teachers' performance. When combined with complementary practices — pre-training compact architectures, aligning intermediate representations, data-centric augmentation, privacy-aware protocols, and task-aware loss design — distillation yields efficient models suitable for real-world NLP and multimodal deployments. However, KD is not a silver bullet: optimization difficulties, capacity mismatch, and data limitations require careful method choices and evaluation. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a central, pragmatic engine of model compression, but one that must be applied with principled, task-aware adjustments to achieve reliable gains in practice.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Ranking Distillation: Learning Compact Ranking Models With High Performance for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel way to train ranking models, such as recommender systems, that are both effective and efficient. Knowledge distillation (KD) was shown to be successful in image recognition to achieve both effectiveness and efficiency. We propose a KD technique for learning to rank problems, called \emph{ranking distillation (RD)}. Specifically, we train a smaller student model to learn to rank documents/items from both the training data and the supervision of a larger teacher model. The student model achieves a similar ranking performance to that of the large teacher model, but its smaller model size makes the online inference more efficient. RD is flexible because it is orthogonal to the choices of ranking models for the teacher and student. We address the challenges of RD for ranking problems. The experiments on public data sets and state-of-the-art recommendation models showed that RD achieves its design purposes: the student model learnt with RD has a model size less than half of the teacher model while achieving a ranking performance similar to the teacher model and much better than the student model learnt without RD.
