papers_seen.author: Zavala
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Limited Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach that enables deploying large models under resource, latency, and privacy constraints by transferring knowledge from teacher to student models. KD extends beyond simple logit matching to include representation-level transfer, attention- and feature-guided objectives, multi-teacher schedules, and integration with architecture search and pretraining. While KD reliably improves efficiency and can preserve many teacher behaviors, its success depends on choices of distillation targets, teacher preparation, student architecture, and data strategies; it can also amplify teacher errors or struggle under data heterogeneity, requiring complementary techniques and careful engineering for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Practical Pathways for Compressing Large NLP Models: Pre-train the Student, Distill Carefully, and Guard for Data & Robustness
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and versatile approach to compress large deep learning models for NLP and related tasks. When the student model is itself pre-trained, distillation yields especially strong and consistent gains; complementary methods — including data augmentation during distillation, progressive module replacement, ensemble teachers or teacher adaptation, and data-free or privacy-aware distillation — address common deployment constraints such as limited task data, inference cost, data access, and adversarial robustness. Combining these techniques and choosing distillation targets and schedules with theoretical and empirical guidance yields compact models that retain much of the original performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Adaptations, and Practical Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques enable deployment of high-performing but large neural models in resource-constrained settings by transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models. Research has developed a spectrum of approaches — from matching logits to feature-level imitation, structural transformation of architectures, multi-teacher schemes, and task-specific adaptations — and has applied them across domains including detection, generative modeling, recommendation, retrieval, and multiple NLP tasks. Empirical work highlights both opportunities (substantial parameter reductions, faster inference, retained or modestly degraded accuracy) and pitfalls (propagation of teacher errors, sensitivity to data heterogeneity, robustness concerns), motivating targeted algorithmic adjustments such as selective distillation, projector modules, and adversarially-aware distillation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Channel Distillation: Channel-Wise Attention for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is to transfer the knowledge from the data learned by the teacher network to the student network, so that the student has the advantage of less parameters and less calculations, and the accuracy is close to the teacher. In this paper, we propose a new distillation method, which contains two transfer distillation strategies and a loss decay strategy. The first transfer strategy is based on channel-wise attention, called Channel Distillation (CD). CD transfers the channel information from the teacher to the student. The second is Guided Knowledge Distillation (GKD). Unlike Knowledge Distillation (KD), which allows the student to mimic each sample's prediction distribution of the teacher, GKD only enables the student to mimic the correct output of the teacher. The last part is Early Decay Teacher (EDT). During the training process, we gradually decay the weight of the distillation loss. The purpose is to enable the student to gradually control the optimization rather than the teacher. Our proposed method is evaluated on ImageNet and CIFAR100. On ImageNet, we achieve 27.68% of top-1 error with ResNet18, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On CIFAR100, we achieve surprising result that the student outperforms the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/zhouzaida/channel-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: A Closer Look at Deep Learning Heuristics: Learning rate restarts, Warmup and Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The convergence rate and final performance of common deep learning models have significantly benefited from heuristics such as learning rate schedules, knowledge distillation, skip connections, and normalization layers. In the absence of theoretical underpinnings, controlled experiments aimed at explaining these strategies can aid our understanding of deep learning landscapes and the training dynamics. Existing approaches for empirical analysis rely on tools of linear interpolation and visualizations with dimensionality reduction, each with their limitations. Instead, we revisit such analysis of heuristics through the lens of recently proposed methods for loss surface and representation analysis, viz., mode connectivity and canonical correlation analysis (CCA), and hypothesize reasons for the success of the heuristics. In particular, we explore knowledge distillation and learning rate heuristics of (cosine) restarts and warmup using mode connectivity and CCA. Our empirical analysis suggests that: (a) the reasons often quoted for the success of cosine annealing are not evidenced in practice; (b) that the effect of learning rate warmup is to prevent the deeper layers from creating training instability; and (c) that the latent knowledge shared by the teacher is primarily disbursed to the deeper layers.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Beyond in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a compression trick but a flexible paradigm that improves efficiency, robustness, privacy, and generalization across modalities and tasks. KD can compress large pretrained models into lightweight deployable models, transfer internal representations to preserve teacher behaviors, operate without original training data, and be adapted to distributed and privacy-sensitive settings. Recent methodological advances—layer- and attention-aware projection, multi-teacher schedules, meta-learned teachers, and techniques connecting KD to regularization—make distillation a practical and theoretically grounded tool for both research and production NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Peters
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central tool for compressing large neural networks so they can run efficiently in production and on resource-constrained devices. Recent work shows KD can preserve much of the teacher performance while reducing inference cost, and that a range of complementary techniques—data augmentation, multi-teacher schedules, internal representation matching, layer alignment, meta-learning of teachers, and robustness-aware objectives—meaningfully improve student quality or transfer desirable properties. At the same time, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on optimization, the choice of teacher/student architectures, and the distributional complexity of the training data. I argue that best practice for KD in deep learning and NLP is to treat it as a family of methods to be combined—augmenting data, distilling intermediate representations, leveraging multiple or adaptive teachers, and explicitly distilling robustness—rather than as a single fixed recipe.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a heuristic for shrinking large models into a fundamental, flexible family of techniques for producing compact, efficient models across vision, speech, and natural language processing. Methods range from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure; variants address constraints such as lack of original data, domain shift, low-precision hardware, and heterogeneous architectures. Empirical work shows distilled students often recover much of teacher performance while enabling deployment under strict latency, memory, or privacy constraints, but success depends on choices about teacher quality, student capacity, data selection or synthesis, and training protocols. Current directions emphasize multi-stage distillation, data- and architecture-aware objectives, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and pre-training; open problems remain around principled teacher selection, robust cross-domain transfer, low-resource and data-free scenarios, and preserving fairness and calibration under compression.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Learning Perception-Aware Agile Flight in Cluttered Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, neural control policies have outperformed existing model-based planning-and-control methods for autonomously navigating quadrotors through cluttered environments in minimum time. However, they are not perception aware, a crucial requirement in vision-based navigation due to the camera's limited field of view and the underactuated nature of a quadrotor. We propose a learning-based system that achieves perception-aware, agile flight in cluttered environments. Our method combines imitation learning with reinforcement learning (RL) by leveraging a privileged learning-by-cheating framework. Using RL, we first train a perception-aware teacher policy with full-state information to fly in minimum time through cluttered environments. Then, we use imitation learning to distill its knowledge into a vision-based student policy that only perceives the environment via a camera. Our approach tightly couples perception and control, showing a significant advantage in computation speed (10 times faster) and success rate. We demonstrate the closed-loop control performance using hardware-in-the-loop simulation.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from Internal Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is typically conducted by training a small model (the student) to mimic a large and cumbersome model (the teacher). The idea is to compress the knowledge from the teacher by using its output probabilities as soft-labels to optimize the student. However, when the teacher is considerably large, there is no guarantee that the internal knowledge of the teacher will be transferred into the student; even if the student closely matches the soft-labels, its internal representations may be considerably different. This internal mismatch can undermine the generalization capabilities originally intended to be transferred from the teacher to the student. In this paper, we propose to distill the internal representations of a large model such as BERT into a simplified version of it. We formulate two ways to distill such representations and various algorithms to conduct the distillation. We experiment with datasets from the GLUE benchmark and consistently show that adding knowledge distillation from internal representations is a more powerful method than only using soft-label distillation.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques aim to transfer predictive behavior from large, expensive models to smaller, faster models so they can be deployed under resource, latency, or privacy constraints. Over the past decade research has produced a taxonomy of distillation mechanisms (logit/soft-target matching, representation or feature imitation, multi-teacher and ensemble-to-student transfers), adaptations for low-data or data-free settings, and combinations of distillation with architecture search and pruning. Empirical work shows that distilled students can recover much of teacher performance at large computational savings, but also highlights practical failure modes: students often do not perfectly match teacher predictive distributions, optimization choices and training data matter strongly, and specialized methods are needed for task-specific or distributed scenarios. Recent advances emphasize multi-stage/multi-teacher schedules, augmentation-aware objectives, online distributed training, and loss formulations that better capture teacher uncertainty; combining these approaches with automated architecture search and structured pruning yields stronger, hardware-aware compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Learning Student-Friendly Teacher Networks for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel knowledge distillation approach to facilitate the transfer of dark knowledge from a teacher to a student. Contrary to most of the existing methods that rely on effective training of student models given pretrained teachers, we aim to learn the teacher models that are friendly to students and, consequently, more appropriate for knowledge transfer. In other words, at the time of optimizing a teacher model, the proposed algorithm learns the student branches jointly to obtain student-friendly representations. Since the main goal of our approach lies in training teacher models and the subsequent knowledge distillation procedure is straightforward, most of the existing knowledge distillation methods can adopt this technique to improve the performance of diverse student models in terms of accuracy and convergence speed. The proposed algorithm demonstrates outstanding accuracy in several well-known knowledge distillation techniques with various combinations of teacher and student models even in the case that their architectures are heterogeneous and there is no prior knowledge about student models at the time of training teacher networks.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Highlight Every Step: Knowledge Distillation via Collaborative Teaching
papers_seen.abstract: High storage and computational costs obstruct deep neural networks to be deployed on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation aims to train a compact student network by transferring knowledge from a larger pre-trained teacher model. However, most existing methods on knowledge distillation ignore the valuable information among training process associated with training results. In this paper, we provide a new Collaborative Teaching Knowledge Distillation (CTKD) strategy which employs two special teachers. Specifically, one teacher trained from scratch (i.e., scratch teacher) assists the student step by step using its temporary outputs. It forces the student to approach the optimal path towards the final logits with high accuracy. The other pre-trained teacher (i.e., expert teacher) guides the student to focus on a critical region which is more useful for the task. The combination of the knowledge from two special teachers can significantly improve the performance of the student network in knowledge distillation. The results of experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and Tiny ImageNet datasets verify that the proposed knowledge distillation method is efficient and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: BERT-EMD: Many-to-Many Layer Mapping for BERT Compression with Earth Mover's Distance
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) have achieved significant success in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, high storage and computational costs obstruct pre-trained language models to be effectively deployed on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose a novel BERT distillation method based on many-to-many layer mapping, which allows each intermediate student layer to learn from any intermediate teacher layers. In this way, our model can learn from different teacher layers adaptively for various NLP tasks. %motivated by the intuition that different NLP tasks require different levels of linguistic knowledge contained in the intermediate layers of BERT. In addition, we leverage Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to compute the minimum cumulative cost that must be paid to transform knowledge from teacher network to student network. EMD enables the effective matching for many-to-many layer mapping. %EMD can be applied to network layers with different sizes and effectively measures semantic distance between the teacher network and student network. Furthermore, we propose a cost attention mechanism to learn the layer weights used in EMD automatically, which is supposed to further improve the model's performance and accelerate convergence time. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger, higher-capacity models (teachers) to smaller, efficient models (students). In practice KD has been applied to compress large pre-trained language models, enable fast inference in NLP, adapt models to new domains or tasks, support heterogeneous and federated settings, and enable data-free scenarios. Approaches differ in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, relational structure), how teachers and students are paired (single vs multi-teacher, jointly trained teachers), and how training data is used or synthesized. Empirical results show KD can substantially reduce model size and latency while preserving much of task performance, but success depends on choices around layer mapping, feature vs. logit supervision, data complexity, and training protocols. Open challenges include handling data heterogeneity, optimizing teacher-student pairings, and ensuring stable distillation without access to original training data.

papers_seen.author: Patterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical, and Evolving Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a core engineering and research paradigm for compressing large models into efficient students while preserving accuracy and desirable behaviors. KD encompasses soft-target transfer, intermediate representation alignment, ensemble-to-single compression, and complementary data- and architecture-aware techniques. When treated as a design problem—choosing which signals to transfer, how to align representations, and how to manage data constraints—KD enables deployment across resource-limited and domain-shifted settings, but open challenges remain in preserving rare-token behaviors, coping with imperfect teachers, and operating without original data.

papers_seen.author: Crosby
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, faster ones by transferring information from one or more teacher models to a student model. Methods range from matching output distributions (soft logits) to aligning internal representations, using ensembles or multiple teachers, conducting distillation without access to original data, and employing self-distillation or teacher-adaptation strategies. Empirical work across vision and language shows that careful choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to manage data constraints determine the trade-offs between efficiency, accuracy, robustness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Robbins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Central Tool for Compressing Deep and NLP Models: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical method to transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models into smaller, faster students, enabling deployment under latency, memory, and data constraints. KD is most effective when integrated with sensible pre-training, representation-level supervision, adaptive teacher strategies, and complementary compression techniques; but it is not a universal solution and can fail when data are limited, teacher and student representations mismatch, or optimization is poorly designed. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a flexible toolbox—applied carefully, combined with other compression methods, and adapted to domain or system constraints—to deliver reliable, high-quality compressed models for deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: Practical Principles for Effective Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. While classic distillation focuses on matching teacher output probabilities, practical compression across modalities and tasks benefits from richer transfer mechanisms: aligning internal representations, selecting task-relevant signals, leveraging data augmentation or synthetic data when real data are scarce, and using adversarial or ensemble strategies to expose diverse and robust teacher knowledge. When combined thoughtfully these methods enable students that are much smaller and faster while retaining or even improving accuracy and robustness on downstream tasks.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, Practical Benefits and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a simple teacher–student logit-matching trick into a broad, practical toolkit for compressing large models and adapting their knowledge to resource- and data-constrained settings. Effective distillation operates at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational signals), interacts strongly with data and augmentation choices, and is most useful when combined with complementary compression methods and careful teacher–student design. While KD often yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance, its success depends on dealing with data availability, domain shift, teacher quality, and optimization dynamics—areas that remain active research directions.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: What Makes a "Good" Data Augmentation in Knowledge Distillation -- A Statistical Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a general neural network training approach that uses a teacher model to guide the student model. Existing works mainly study KD from the network output side (e.g., trying to design a better KD loss function), while few have attempted to understand it from the input side. Especially, its interplay with data augmentation (DA) has not been well understood. In this paper, we ask: Why do some DA schemes (e.g., CutMix) inherently perform much better than others in KD? What makes a "good" DA in KD? Our investigation from a statistical perspective suggests that a good DA scheme should reduce the covariance of the teacher-student cross-entropy. A practical metric, the stddev of teacher's mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Extensive empirical studies support our claims and demonstrate how we can harvest considerable performance gains simply by using a better DA scheme in knowledge distillation.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Tool for Practical Model Compression across Modalities
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic for transferring soft logits to a rich family of techniques that enable deployment of large models in resource-constrained settings. Across NLP, vision, generative modeling, and cross-modal systems, distillation methods that match intermediate representations, adapt teacher signals to student inputs, exploit many-to-many layer correspondences, and combine with pruning or ensemble guidance consistently produce compact models with near-teacher performance. KD is also effective for domain adaptation and continual learning, making it a practical foundation for producing small, fast, and robust models for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: TRILLsson: Distilled Universal Paralinguistic Speech Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in self-supervision have dramatically improved the quality of speech representations. However, deployment of state-of-the-art embedding models on devices has been restricted due to their limited public availability and large resource footprint. Our work addresses these issues by publicly releasing a collection of paralinguistic speech models that are small and near state-of-the-art performance. Our approach is based on knowledge distillation, and our models are distilled on public data only. We explore different architectures and thoroughly evaluate our models on the Non-Semantic Speech (NOSS) benchmark. Our largest distilled model is less than 15% the size of the original model (314MB vs 2.2GB), achieves over 96% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks, and is trained on 6.5% the data. The smallest model is 1% in size (22MB) and achieves over 90% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks. Our models outperform the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 model on 6 of 7 tasks, and our smallest model outperforms the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 on both emotion recognition tasks despite being 7% the size.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, faster models while retaining much of their performance. Across modalities and tasks—language understanding, machine translation, reading comprehension, and large-scale distributed training—recent work shows KD can improve inference speed, aid domain adaptation, enable training without original data, and increase robustness. Combining innovations in layer mapping, feature-level transfer, online and data-free techniques, and teacher optimization yields the best trade-offs for real deployments.

papers_seen.author: Chapman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly used technique to transfer information from larger or more complex models to smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained models. It serves both model compression and training-stabilization roles across vision, speech, and language tasks. KD variants include offline teacher-student distillation, online/co-distillation among peers, feature- and representation-level matching, and hybrid schemes that combine distillation with quantization or specialized training objectives. Empirical evidence shows KD can improve accuracy, generalization, robustness, and inference efficiency, but its success depends on data complexity, teacher design, and the type of knowledge transferred.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression strategies enable deployment of large pretrained models by transferring function or representation from larger (teacher) models to smaller (student) ones. Across supervised, self-supervised, and data-free settings, KD methods exploit soft targets, intermediate representation matching, architectural surgery, and data or training-time modifications to improve student accuracy, robustness, or efficiency. Empirical results show that appropriately designed distillation can retain most teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in model size, precision, or inference cost; but effectiveness depends on choices of targets, data, and teacher-student compatibility. Open challenges include preserving rare-token behavior in distilled NLP models, mitigating bias transfer, and jointly optimizing hardware constraints and task performance.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment. Research over the past decade has produced a wide array of distillation variants (logit-based supervision, feature and attention matching, multi- and self-distillation, data-free methods) and shown how KD can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet practical constraints. Empirical and theoretical work identifies both the strengths of KD (regularization, practical deployment gains, domain adaptation) and its limits (optimization difficulty, capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors), motivating a pragmatic set of design choices for robust compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Effective Practices and Practical Recommendations for Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and model compression are practical, versatile tools for deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Across computer vision, multimodal, and natural language processing tasks, distillation can preserve or approximate teacher performance while substantially reducing model size and latency. Successful distillation strategies go beyond matching final logits: they exploit intermediate representations, task-aware selection of teacher signals, many-to-many layer mappings, and feature-level or adversarial training to transfer richer knowledge. Combining these approaches yields compact models that retain robustness and task performance, and that can be further complemented by pruning or hardware-aware compression for deployment.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression and Robust Deployment in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach to compressing large models into smaller, faster models while preserving— and in some settings improving—accuracy, robustness, and domain suitability. KD can be adapted to resource-constrained deployment, domain adaptation, privacy- or data-limited settings, and to improve adversarial robustness when paired with targeted techniques. Combining KD with complementary compression methods (e.g., pruning, structured sparsity, layer mapping) yields practical, high-quality compressed models across modalities including vision, language, graphs, and generative models.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, faster models while retaining much of their performance. Across modalities and tasks—language understanding, machine translation, reading comprehension, and large-scale distributed training—recent work shows KD can improve inference speed, aid domain adaptation, enable training without original data, and increase robustness. Combining innovations in layer mapping, feature-level transfer, online and data-free techniques, and teacher optimization yields the best trade-offs for real deployments.

papers_seen.author: Freeman
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core technique for producing compact, deployable neural models by transferring predictive behavior or internal structure from larger teacher models to smaller students. KD encompasses a spectrum of objectives — from matching soft output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, relational statistics, or task-specific features — and it is often combined with architectural modification, pruning, quantization, or data synthesis to meet deployment constraints. Practical KD addresses data scarcity, domain shift, heterogeneity of devices and architectures, and privacy concerns through strategies such as data-free distillation, multi-teacher weighting, teacher adaptation, and curriculum or instance-aware sampling. While KD routinely yields large efficiency gains with modest accuracy loss, careful design is needed to avoid capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher biases, and degradation on rare or out-of-domain inputs.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile technique that enables compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teachers' performance. When combined with complementary practices — pre-training compact architectures, aligning intermediate representations, data-centric augmentation, privacy-aware protocols, and task-aware loss design — distillation yields efficient models suitable for real-world NLP and multimodal deployments. However, KD is not a silver bullet: optimization difficulties, capacity mismatch, and data limitations require careful method choices and evaluation. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a central, pragmatic engine of model compression, but one that must be applied with principled, task-aware adjustments to achieve reliable gains in practice.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Contemporary Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural relationships. Across computer vision and natural language processing, a wide family of distillation strategies—ranging from soft-label (logit) matching to feature- and attention-level imitation, multi-teacher and online schemes, many-to-many layer mappings, and task-aware layer selection—has been developed to trade off accuracy, latency, and model size for practical deployment. Empirical work shows that combining distillation with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware transformations) and adapting distillation signals to task and data constraints yields compact models that capture much of teacher performance. At the same time, distillation must contend with capacity mismatch, robustness and distribution-shift sensitivity, privacy concerns, and the need for principled layer- and signal-alignment strategies—areas that motivate continued methodological and theoretical work.

papers_seen.author: Ball
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical but Nuanced Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach to compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones. When used thoughtfully, KD can preserve much of a teacher's performance while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. However, distillation is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on which signals are transferred (logits, features, relational information), alignment between teacher and student, availability or synthesis of suitable data, and awareness of teacher imperfections. Combining KD with representation-level matching, task-aware layer alignment, online or federated protocols, and data strategies yields the best trade-offs for real systems.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: BERT-EMD: Many-to-Many Layer Mapping for BERT Compression with Earth Mover's Distance
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) have achieved significant success in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, high storage and computational costs obstruct pre-trained language models to be effectively deployed on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose a novel BERT distillation method based on many-to-many layer mapping, which allows each intermediate student layer to learn from any intermediate teacher layers. In this way, our model can learn from different teacher layers adaptively for various NLP tasks. %motivated by the intuition that different NLP tasks require different levels of linguistic knowledge contained in the intermediate layers of BERT. In addition, we leverage Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to compute the minimum cumulative cost that must be paid to transform knowledge from teacher network to student network. EMD enables the effective matching for many-to-many layer mapping. %EMD can be applied to network layers with different sizes and effectively measures semantic distance between the teacher network and student network. Furthermore, we propose a cost attention mechanism to learn the layer weights used in EMD automatically, which is supposed to further improve the model's performance and accelerate convergence time. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Nuanced Path to Model Compression in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques to transfer knowledge from large teacher models into smaller students, enabling deployment under resource, latency, and privacy constraints. When combined with complementary strategies — such as pre-training compact architectures, data augmentation, selective sample transfer, and module-level compression — KD can yield compact models that retain much of the teacher's utility. However, distillation is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on what is transferred, the availability and nature of data, teacher–student design, and optimization choices. Responsible deployment requires understanding both the practical strengths (efficiency, adaptability, applicability to privacy settings) and the limitations (data dependence, optimization gaps, possible degradation on rare or shifted inputs) of distillation methods.

papers_seen.author: Fletcher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable strategy for transferring information from larger, often over-parameterized teacher models into smaller, faster student models to enable deployment under constraints of latency, memory, data access, or privacy. KD techniques span output-level supervision (soft logits), intermediate representation matching, multi-teacher and ensemble strategies, self- and progressive distillation, and data-free or zero-shot variants. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance across modalities (vision, speech, translation, detection, and generation) while enabling on-device and real-time use; success depends on the choice of distillation targets, the match between teacher and student capacity, the availability and quality of data, and appropriate regularization or augmentation during training. Practical deployment typically combines KD with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and privacy-aware mechanisms to produce robust compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Holmes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches and Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of their performance. Work across NLP and broader deep learning has developed multiple KD paradigms—soft-label (logit) matching, intermediate-representation matching, layer-to-layer and many-to-many layer mapping, multi-teacher aggregation, and data-free distillation—and combined KD with other compression methods such as quantization, pruning, and architecture search. Empirical results show that well-designed distillation can yield compact models that approach the accuracy of large pre-trained models while offering substantial savings in parameters, latency, and computational cost. Remaining challenges include aligning heterogeneous teacher and student architectures, coping with limited or unavailable training data, and selecting or weighting multiple teachers per example. The literature suggests principled strategies—attention-based layer fusion, representation-level losses, teacher confidence or dynamic weighting, and synthetic-data generation—that mitigate these issues and enable effective deployment of compressed models in domain-specific and resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Yu
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: Toward Integrated Feature-, Data- and Robustness-aware Knowledge Distillation for Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has matured from simple logit matching into a toolbox of complementary techniques. Empirical and theoretical work shows that (1) matching internal features often transfers richer representations than logits alone, (2) the choice of input-side interventions (e.g., data augmentation) substantially changes distillation dynamics, and (3) robustness, teacher quality, and sample selection must be addressed explicitly. I argue that effective model compression in deep learning and NLP requires integrating feature-level mimicry with careful input-space design, selective or confidence-weighted teacher signals, and robustness-aware objectives. This combined approach maximizes student performance while keeping models compact and deployment-ready.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Distilling the Knowledge of BERT for Sequence-to-Sequence ASR
papers_seen.abstract: Attention-based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models have achieved promising results in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, as these models decode in a left-to-right way, they do not have access to context on the right. We leverage both left and right context by applying BERT as an external language model to seq2seq ASR through knowledge distillation. In our proposed method, BERT generates soft labels to guide the training of seq2seq ASR. Furthermore, we leverage context beyond the current utterance as input to BERT. Experimental evaluations show that our method significantly improves the ASR performance from the seq2seq baseline on the Corpus of Spontaneous Japanese (CSJ). Knowledge distillation from BERT outperforms that from a transformer LM that only looks at left context. We also show the effectiveness of leveraging context beyond the current utterance. Our method outperforms other LM application approaches such as n-best rescoring and shallow fusion, while it does not require extra inference cost.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach to convert large, accurate models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—choosing what teacher signals to transfer, aligning mismatched architectures, and addressing data constraints—KD can preserve most teacher performance while enabling orders-of-magnitude improvements in latency, memory footprint, and deployability. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on representations transferred, the provenance and augmentation of distillation data, and deployment constraints such as privacy or distributed training. Effective compression therefore treats KD as a core tool within a broader toolkit that includes feature-level alignment, data-aware strategies, online or multi-teacher setups, and data-free techniques when real data are unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Velasquez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Multifaceted Tool Beyond Simple Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be understood and applied as a flexible toolbox rather than merely a compression trick. KD enables compression, regularization, privacy-preserving transfer, and adaptation across diverse constraints (data scarcity, heterogeneous devices, federated settings). Effective practice combines soft-target supervision with representation-level alignment, architecture-aware methods (pruning, quantization, search), and privacy-aware or teacher-free variants. However, careful design is required to avoid capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, and robustness or bias degradation.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger, higher-capacity models (teachers) to smaller, efficient models (students). In practice KD has been applied to compress large pre-trained language models, enable fast inference in NLP, adapt models to new domains or tasks, support heterogeneous and federated settings, and enable data-free scenarios. Approaches differ in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, relational structure), how teachers and students are paired (single vs multi-teacher, jointly trained teachers), and how training data is used or synthesized. Empirical results show KD can substantially reduce model size and latency while preserving much of task performance, but success depends on choices around layer mapping, feature vs. logit supervision, data complexity, and training protocols. Open challenges include handling data heterogeneity, optimizing teacher-student pairings, and ensuring stable distillation without access to original training data.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: Practical Principles for Effective Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. While classic distillation focuses on matching teacher output probabilities, practical compression across modalities and tasks benefits from richer transfer mechanisms: aligning internal representations, selecting task-relevant signals, leveraging data augmentation or synthetic data when real data are scarce, and using adversarial or ensemble strategies to expose diverse and robust teacher knowledge. When combined thoughtfully these methods enable students that are much smaller and faster while retaining or even improving accuracy and robustness on downstream tasks.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Unifying Tool: Beyond Compression to Privacy, Robustness, Fairness, and Theory
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation began as a technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, faster models, but its utility now spans privacy-preserving training, robustness transfer, fairness mitigation, domain generalization, and theoretical insights about learning. Distillation can (1) produce compact models that retain most of a teacher's performance, (2) transfer nontrivial inductive biases and robustness properties, and (3) be adapted to settings with privacy constraints or imperfect teachers. However, distillation is not a panacea: teacher errors, choice of distilled data, and sample-level effects can harm the student unless carefully managed. This perspective synthesizes empirical and theoretical evidence to argue that knowledge distillation is a central, flexible methodology for modern deep learning, while highlighting practical constraints and directions for responsible application.

papers_seen.author: Carney
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses and transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models to improve efficiency while retaining performance. Methods span logits-based soft-label transfer, feature- or layer-wise matching, adversarial and data-free distillation, architecture-aware projection or search, and task-adaptive compression for NLP. Empirical work shows KD is effective across vision, speech, generative models, and language models; recent theory clarifies when and why soft labels help and when mixing hard labels matters. Practical designs—attention-guided layer alignment, projectors or ensembles of projectors, and careful data augmentation or synthetic-data generation—substantially affect student quality. Open challenges include data-privacy constraints, distillation across heterogeneous architectures, preserving teacher errors, and better theoretical/empirical guidance for designing KD pipelines for diverse tasks.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: The Central Role and Evolving Practices of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental and versatile approach for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP. It enables compact, efficient student models that retain much of a teacher's performance, supports deployment on resource-constrained devices, and can be adapted to privacy-sensitive or distributed settings. Recent advances extend distillation beyond simple logits matching to many-to-many layer mapping, task-adaptive compression, teacher-aware training, adversarial and data-free scenarios, and robustness-aware objectives. Together these developments show that distillation is both a practical engineering tool and a rich research paradigm for addressing capacity, data availability, privacy, and robustness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is the most pragmatic and versatile route to make large deep models usable in constrained settings. When treated as a flexible toolkit—not merely as soft-label matching—KD enables compact models that preserve student performance, transfer intermediate representations, and support deployment constraints such as limited data, heterogeneous devices, or low-precision inference. Real-world success requires combining KD with task-aware layer mapping, multi-teacher or ensemble signals, data-generation or adversarial synthesis when original data are unavailable, and joint use with quantization or precision-reduction. These combinations produce students that are both efficient and robust enough for production use.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques provide a broad, practically oriented toolkit for shrinking large neural models while retaining most of their performance. Methods include transferring soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, adapting teacher or student architectures, using adversarial or data-free sample generation, and combining distillation with quantization or pruning. Empirical results across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks show substantial latency and memory gains; success depends on what signals are transferred, how layers are matched, data availability and augmentation, and the deployment constraints that shape algorithmic choices.

papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Multifaceted Strategy for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep and NLP models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Beyond matching final outputs, modern KD variants transfer intermediate representations, adapt teacher behavior to students, and operate when task data are limited or unavailable. KD is most effective when combined with task-aware signal selection, teacher design, data strategies, and complementary compression such as architecture search or pruning; used in this way, KD enables compact models that approach teacher performance while addressing real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Archer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for producing compact, efficient models from larger teachers. KD can preserve predictive performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Its strengths derive from a variety of mechanisms — soft-label matching, internal-feature alignment, layer-mapping, and task-adaptive architecture design — and from being combinable with complementary compression techniques. However, realizing consistent gains requires careful choice of distilled targets, attention to representation alignment between teacher and student, and explicit handling of data-, fairness-, and robustness-related risks. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a toolbox of targeted interventions rather than a single recipe, and provides concise, evidence-based recommendations for practitioners compressing models in vision and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and widely applicable paradigm for compressing large models and transferring knowledge across architectures, tasks, and deployment constraints. A range of KD variants—data-free, federated, multi-teacher, meta-learned teachers, intermediate-feature transfer, and architecture-aware compression—have been developed to address realistic constraints such as data privacy, limited communication, teacher imperfection, and task-specific efficiency. By matching the KD strategy to the deployment constraint (e.g., privacy, compute budget, domain shift, or paucity of data) practitioners can obtain compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency and resource requirements.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. The literature has expanded beyond soft-label matching to include intermediate representation imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, multi- and adaptive-teacher schemes, data- and domain-aware protocols, and combinations with pruning or architecture search. Empirical work shows KD can preserve a large fraction of teacher performance across vision and language tasks, while theoretical and empirical analyses clarify when distillation helps, how teacher quality and data regimes affect outcomes, and what practical trade-offs remain. Open problems center on robustness to domain shift and adversaries, distillation without original data, and automated, architecture-agnostic pipelines for production systems.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Learning Student-Friendly Teacher Networks for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel knowledge distillation approach to facilitate the transfer of dark knowledge from a teacher to a student. Contrary to most of the existing methods that rely on effective training of student models given pretrained teachers, we aim to learn the teacher models that are friendly to students and, consequently, more appropriate for knowledge transfer. In other words, at the time of optimizing a teacher model, the proposed algorithm learns the student branches jointly to obtain student-friendly representations. Since the main goal of our approach lies in training teacher models and the subsequent knowledge distillation procedure is straightforward, most of the existing knowledge distillation methods can adopt this technique to improve the performance of diverse student models in terms of accuracy and convergence speed. The proposed algorithm demonstrates outstanding accuracy in several well-known knowledge distillation techniques with various combinations of teacher and student models even in the case that their architectures are heterogeneous and there is no prior knowledge about student models at the time of training teacher networks.
