papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and model compression techniques compress or replace large pretrained models with smaller, efficient models while aiming to retain much of the original performance. Modern work spans logit-based soft-label distillation, feature- and attention-based representation matching, layer-wise and task-aware alignment, online and mutual distillation schemes, meta-learned teachers, and approaches for resource- or data-constrained scenarios (including data-free and few-shot settings). Applications include compressing large language models into lightweight architectures for deployment, accelerating visual and multimodal models, enabling distributed training, and improving robustness and transfer. Key challenges include selecting what to transfer (logits vs. features), how to align heterogeneous architectures, preventing capacity mismatch and overfitting, and preserving task-relevant information while removing redundant representations. Empirical strategies that combine representation-level losses, task-aware selection, and online or meta-learning mechanisms tend to yield the best tradeoffs between efficiency and retained accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical, but Nuanced Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically proven approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones while preserving much of their performance. KD can operate at multiple levels (soft logits, intermediate features, relational structure) and be combined with complementary compression techniques, data synthesis, or student-aware teacher training to meet deployment constraints in vision, language, and graph domains. However, its success depends on careful design choices — what to transfer, how to map teacher and student layers, how to handle limited or private data, and whether to adapt the teacher — and practitioners should treat KD as part of a broader compression toolkit rather than a universal solution.

papers_seen.author: Hamilton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Core for Model Compression with Clear Limits and Research Priorities
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones across vision, speech, and language. KD combines multiple signals (soft-labels, intermediate representations, attention and feature matching, synthetic-data generation) and integrates naturally with complementary compression methods. However, its practical success depends on careful teacher–student design, access to appropriate data (or robust data-free methods), and mitigation of optimization, robustness, and fairness risks. This paper argues that KD should remain central to compression pipelines while research focuses on principled teacher selection, reliable data-free distillation, representation-aware objectives, and safeguards for privacy and bias.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: The Case for Practical, Adaptive Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible tool for compressing large deep learning models into deployable students. Recent work shows KD can both directly reduce model size and serve as a mechanism to transfer inductive biases, intermediate representations, and task-specific attention. However, real-world constraints — limited or private training data, domain and client heterogeneity, and redundant teacher representations — require KD methods that are data-free, adversarially robust, task-aware, and selective about what teacher knowledge to transfer.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation unifies multiple strategies for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable models while preserving performance. It supports a range of goals — parameter and latency reduction, robustness, interpretability, and privacy-aware deployment — by transferring information from a teacher to a student via soft outputs, intermediate representations, or structural/architectural guidance. Practical and research advances show that combining distillation modes (feature-level, output-level, progressive module replacement), data augmentation, and adaptive teacher training yields compact models that approach teacher performance even under limited data, heterogeneous devices, or privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile tool for transferring functionality from large, expensive models to smaller, more efficient ones across modalities. When properly applied, KD can enable deployment of compact models with competitive accuracy, but its effectiveness depends on dataset complexity, selection of distilled signals, and complementary compression strategies. This paper synthesizes empirical findings and method-level advances to argue for principled, task-aware KD workflows that mitigate common pitfalls while maximizing compression gains.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Scott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, and Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates through multiple mechanisms—matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational structure, and providing regularization—that together enable substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. KD integrates naturally with other compression methods (architecture search, pruning, quantization), supports data-free and privacy-sensitive settings, and scales across modalities and deployment constraints. At the same time, effective distillation requires careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to map teacher and student layers, how to handle imperfect teachers and data mismatch, and when to combine KD with complementary techniques. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a toolbox rather than a single recipe and offers practical, evidence-based recommendations for deploying KD in real systems.

papers_seen.author: Allison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Necessity for Deploying Large NLP and Deep Learning Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster models while retaining much of their performance. Beyond simple logit matching, modern distillation encompasses feature-level mimicry, teacher adaptation, task-adaptive compression, data-free and privacy-aware approaches, and continual or online schemes to maintain performance over time or across domains. When applied thoughtfully—choosing appropriate teacher signals, intermediate-target losses, and deployment-aware architecture search—KD enables real-world use of large pretrained models in latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: TextKD-GAN: Text Generation using KnowledgeDistillation and Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Text generation is of particular interest in many NLP applications such as machine translation, language modeling, and text summarization. Generative adversarial networks (GANs) achieved a remarkable success in high quality image generation in computer vision,and recently, GANs have gained lots of interest from the NLP community as well. However, achieving similar success in NLP would be more challenging due to the discrete nature of text. In this work, we introduce a method using knowledge distillation to effectively exploit GAN setup for text generation. We demonstrate how autoencoders (AEs) can be used for providing a continuous representation of sentences, which is a smooth representation that assign non-zero probabilities to more than one word. We distill this representation to train the generator to synthesize similar smooth representations. We perform a number of experiments to validate our idea using different datasets and show that our proposed approach yields better performance in terms of the BLEU score and Jensen-Shannon distance (JSD) measure compared to traditional GAN-based text generation approaches without pre-training.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Adversarially Robust Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is effective for producing small, high-performance neural networks for classification, but these small networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper studies how adversarial robustness transfers from teacher to student during knowledge distillation. We find that a large amount of robustness may be inherited by the student even when distilled on only clean images. Second, we introduce Adversarially Robust Distillation (ARD) for distilling robustness onto student networks. In addition to producing small models with high test accuracy like conventional distillation, ARD also passes the superior robustness of large networks onto the student. In our experiments, we find that ARD student models decisively outperform adversarially trained networks of identical architecture in terms of robust accuracy, surpassing state-of-the-art methods on standard robustness benchmarks. Finally, we adapt recent fast adversarial training methods to ARD for accelerated robust distillation.

papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Multifaceted Strategy for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep and NLP models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Beyond matching final outputs, modern KD variants transfer intermediate representations, adapt teacher behavior to students, and operate when task data are limited or unavailable. KD is most effective when combined with task-aware signal selection, teacher design, data strategies, and complementary compression such as architecture search or pruning; used in this way, KD enables compact models that approach teacher performance while addressing real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Estes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Toolbox: Principles, Limits, and Practical Prescriptions for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation should be understood and applied as a flexible set of techniques that go well beyond simple parameter compression. When treated as a toolbox—combining soft-target supervision, internal representation matching, layer-aware alignment, attention-guided mapping, and complementary compression methods—distillation can produce compact models that preserve accuracy, improve interpretability, and transfer robustness or privacy properties. Success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to prepare the student, and how to mitigate propagation of teacher defects; practitioners benefit from system-level designs that pair distillation objectives with pre-training, data augmentation, and architecture-aware compression.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central strategy for compressing large neural networks into compact, deployable models across computer vision, generative modeling, and natural language processing. KD techniques extend beyond matching teacher output probabilities to include distillation of intermediate representations, layer-level mappings, and training without access to original data. Practical applications span compressing generative adversarial networks, pre-trained language models, and low-precision networks, while also addressing robustness and privacy constraints. Empirical work shows that carefully designed distillation protocols can retain most of a teacher's performance or even improve downstream robustness and inference efficiency, though success depends on choices such as what knowledge to transfer, architectural alignment, and availability of data or suitable synthetic surrogates.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques are widely used to transfer behavior from large teacher models to smaller students, enabling deployment under resource constraints. Research over the past decade has developed variants that target outputs (soft labels), internal representations (layer-wise and attention-based methods), data regimes (data-free or distilled training sets), and architecture search for task-aware compression. Empirical and theoretical work highlights both the practical gains and fundamental limits of distillation, and points to best practices such as pre-training compact models, selecting or synthesizing appropriate training data, and aligning student capacity to distilled signal.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression strategies enable deployment of large pretrained models by transferring function or representation from larger (teacher) models to smaller (student) ones. Across supervised, self-supervised, and data-free settings, KD methods exploit soft targets, intermediate representation matching, architectural surgery, and data or training-time modifications to improve student accuracy, robustness, or efficiency. Empirical results show that appropriately designed distillation can retain most teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in model size, precision, or inference cost; but effectiveness depends on choices of targets, data, and teacher-student compatibility. Open challenges include preserving rare-token behavior in distilled NLP models, mitigating bias transfer, and jointly optimizing hardware constraints and task performance.

papers_seen.author: Zamora
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression strategies aim to transfer predictive behavior from larger or more expensive models to smaller, faster, or more resource-efficient ones. The literature shows a variety of mechanisms (soft-label supervision, intermediate-feature alignment, progressive module replacement, adversarial feature matching), data- and training-focused interventions (data selection, augmentation, mixup, control of dataset complexity), and hybrid combinations with pruning or ensembling. Empirical results across NLP and vision tasks indicate that KD can preserve much of teacher performance while accelerating inference, but success depends strongly on (a) the choice of distillation targets and layer mappings, (b) the complexity and provenance of the distillation data, and (c) complementary techniques such as pre-training, feature-level matching, or structured pruning. Practical approaches therefore tailor the distillation recipe to model capacity, task characteristics, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression strategies have become central for deploying high-performing deep models under resource, latency, and privacy constraints. Research has developed a spectrum of techniques — from soft-target supervision and intermediate-layer transfer to multi-teacher, data-free, and federated variants — and combined distillation with pruning and architecture search to compress large transformers and other architectures. Empirical and theoretical work highlights both practical gains (speed, memory, privacy) and fundamental tradeoffs (bias–variance, data heterogeneity, and information loss), pointing to hybrid protocols and adaptive selection of distillation signals as promising directions.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Challenges, and Practical Advances
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller students by transferring predictive behavior or intermediate representations. Research has developed many variants — logits-based soft-labels, feature- and attention-based matching, layer-wise and task-aware filters, self-distillation, and data-free approaches — and applied them across vision, language, recommendation, and healthcare. Empirical and theoretical work highlights both the practical benefits (faster inference, lower memory, domain adaptation, interpretability) and core limitations (optimization obstacles, capacity mismatch, distributional effects), motivating techniques that alter what is distilled, how it is matched, and even how teachers are trained to be more amenable to students.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not a mere optimization trick but a central, versatile toolkit for compressing large models into compact, deployable students. When treated as a system composed of complementary ingredients—teacher design (single, ensemble or multi-teacher), what to transfer (logits, intermediate representations, relational information), how to obtain data (real, synthesized, or data-free), and deployment constraints (privacy, federated or on-device latency)—KD consistently enables strong trade-offs between efficiency and performance across vision, language, generative, and real-world production tasks. Realizing KD’s full potential requires representation- and layer-aware objectives, adaptive teacher–student mappings, careful handling of data scarcity or privacy, and integration with pretraining and other compression methods.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach to convert large, accurate models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—choosing what teacher signals to transfer, aligning mismatched architectures, and addressing data constraints—KD can preserve most teacher performance while enabling orders-of-magnitude improvements in latency, memory footprint, and deployability. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on representations transferred, the provenance and augmentation of distillation data, and deployment constraints such as privacy or distributed training. Effective compression therefore treats KD as a core tool within a broader toolkit that includes feature-level alignment, data-aware strategies, online or multi-teacher setups, and data-free techniques when real data are unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Towards Efficient 3D Object Detection with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite substantial progress in 3D object detection, advanced 3D detectors often suffer from heavy computation overheads. To this end, we explore the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) for developing efficient 3D object detectors, focusing on popular pillar- and voxel-based detectors.In the absence of well-developed teacher-student pairs, we first study how to obtain student models with good trade offs between accuracy and efficiency from the perspectives of model compression and input resolution reduction. Then, we build a benchmark to assess existing KD methods developed in the 2D domain for 3D object detection upon six well-constructed teacher-student pairs. Further, we propose an improved KD pipeline incorporating an enhanced logit KD method that performs KD on only a few pivotal positions determined by teacher classification response, and a teacher-guided student model initialization to facilitate transferring teacher model's feature extraction ability to students through weight inheritance. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on the Waymo dataset. Our best performing model achieves $65.75\%$ LEVEL 2 mAPH, surpassing its teacher model and requiring only $44\%$ of teacher flops. Our most efficient model runs 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, which is $2.2\times$ faster than PointPillar with even higher accuracy. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD}.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: VPN++: Rethinking Video-Pose embeddings for understanding Activities of Daily Living
papers_seen.abstract: Many attempts have been made towards combining RGB and 3D poses for the recognition of Activities of Daily Living (ADL). ADL may look very similar and often necessitate to model fine-grained details to distinguish them. Because the recent 3D ConvNets are too rigid to capture the subtle visual patterns across an action, this research direction is dominated by methods combining RGB and 3D Poses. But the cost of computing 3D poses from RGB stream is high in the absence of appropriate sensors. This limits the usage of aforementioned approaches in real-world applications requiring low latency. Then, how to best take advantage of 3D Poses for recognizing ADL? To this end, we propose an extension of a pose driven attention mechanism: Video-Pose Network (VPN), exploring two distinct directions. One is to transfer the Pose knowledge into RGB through a feature-level distillation and the other towards mimicking pose driven attention through an attention-level distillation. Finally, these two approaches are integrated into a single model, we call VPN++. We show that VPN++ is not only effective but also provides a high speed up and high resilience to noisy Poses. VPN++, with or without 3D Poses, outperforms the representative baselines on 4 public datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/srijandas07/vpnplusplus.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Revisiting Knowledge Distillation via Label Smoothing Regularization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to distill the knowledge of a cumbersome teacher model into a lightweight student model. Its success is generally attributed to the privileged information on similarities among categories provided by the teacher model, and in this sense, only strong teacher models are deployed to teach weaker students in practice. In this work, we challenge this common belief by following experimental observations: 1) beyond the acknowledgment that the teacher can improve the student, the student can also enhance the teacher significantly by reversing the KD procedure; 2) a poorly-trained teacher with much lower accuracy than the student can still improve the latter significantly. To explain these observations, we provide a theoretical analysis of the relationships between KD and label smoothing regularization. We prove that 1) KD is a type of learned label smoothing regularization and 2) label smoothing regularization provides a virtual teacher model for KD. From these results, we argue that the success of KD is not fully due to the similarity information between categories from teachers, but also to the regularization of soft targets, which is equally or even more important.   Based on these analyses, we further propose a novel Teacher-free Knowledge Distillation (Tf-KD) framework, where a student model learns from itself or manuallydesigned regularization distribution. The Tf-KD achieves comparable performance with normal KD from a superior teacher, which is well applied when a stronger teacher model is unavailable. Meanwhile, Tf-KD is generic and can be directly deployed for training deep neural networks. Without any extra computation cost, Tf-KD achieves up to 0.65\% improvement on ImageNet over well-established baseline models, which is superior to label smoothing regularization.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Compressing Deep and NLP Models: Methods, Limits, and Complementary Techniques
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a core strategy to compress large pre-trained deep models so they can be deployed in latency- and resource-constrained settings. KD variants—multi-teacher pipelines, layer-wise and task-aware alignment, self-distillation, and feature-level matching—enable small students to approach or match teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost. KD is most effective when combined with complementary approaches such as pruning and architecture search, and when adapted to domain or system constraints (e.g., federated or multi-device settings). However, KD is not a universal panacea: data heterogeneity, misaligned inputs between teacher and student, and inappropriate augmentation or feature transfer can limit gains, so careful design choices are required to realize practical compression.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Beyond in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a compression trick but a flexible paradigm that improves efficiency, robustness, privacy, and generalization across modalities and tasks. KD can compress large pretrained models into lightweight deployable models, transfer internal representations to preserve teacher behaviors, operate without original training data, and be adapted to distributed and privacy-sensitive settings. Recent methodological advances—layer- and attention-aware projection, multi-teacher schedules, meta-learned teachers, and techniques connecting KD to regularization—make distillation a practical and theoretically grounded tool for both research and production NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Partial Solution for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile means to compress large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their teacher performance. In practice KD enables latency- and memory-constrained deployment, supports continual and domain adaptation, and can be combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet engineering constraints. However, KD is not a panacea: it can propagate teacher errors, struggle with low-frequency or fine-grained behaviors, and requires task-aware alignment of signals and data strategies (including privacy-preserving or data-free approaches) to realize consistent benefits. I argue KD should be treated as a flexible toolkit that is integrated with task-aware layer mapping, privacy and data strategies, and complementary compression methods to produce robust, high-utility compressed models for NLP and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and adaptable family of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster models suitable for deployment. Beyond the classic teacher-logit supervision, modern distillation covers feature-level matching, task-adaptive architecture search, multi-teacher transfer, and data-free scenarios. KD can be combined with pruning and structured sparsity, adapted for domain shifts, and used to transfer ensemble or task-specific knowledge into compact models. The choice of distillation target, the availability of data, and the deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy, domain) determine which distillation recipe will be most effective.

papers_seen.author: Jacobs
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure. It has evolved from straightforward soft-label training to richer objectives that match features, attention, or module behaviors, and to deployment-aware variants that address privacy, data scarcity, and heterogeneous devices. Empirical work across vision and language shows distilled students can approach teacher performance when distillation signals, data, and architecture choices are carefully matched; important open problems include data heterogeneity, capacity mismatch, bias transfer, and theoretical understanding of what is actually transferred.

papers_seen.author: Cruz
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable paradigm for transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller, more efficient students. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, KD methods—ranging from matching teacher output distributions to aligning intermediate representations and relational structure—enable substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to obtain or synthesize training data, and whether to complement distillation with adversarial or ensemble signals. When these elements are chosen and tuned for task and deployment constraints, KD produces compact models that are effective in resource-limited and application-specific settings.

papers_seen.author: Oliver
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core of Model Compression: Effectiveness, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and NLP. When combined with complementary practices—task-aware signal selection, intermediate representation alignment, pretraining for compact architectures, multi-teacher or self-distillation, and data augmentation or synthesis—KD can yield compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency and resource constraints. However, KD is not a universal solution: data availability, teacher–student heterogeneity, fairness concerns, and theoretical gaps constrain its effectiveness in some settings. Careful design choices and hybrid pipelines are therefore required to realize reliable compression in production systems.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: ALP-KD: Attention-Based Layer Projection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is considered as a training and compression strategy in which two neural networks, namely a teacher and a student, are coupled together during training. The teacher network is supposed to be a trustworthy predictor and the student tries to mimic its predictions. Usually, a student with a lighter architecture is selected so we can achieve compression and yet deliver high-quality results. In such a setting, distillation only happens for final predictions whereas the student could also benefit from teacher's supervision for internal components.   Motivated by this, we studied the problem of distillation for intermediate layers. Since there might not be a one-to-one alignment between student and teacher layers, existing techniques skip some teacher layers and only distill from a subset of them. This shortcoming directly impacts quality, so we instead propose a combinatorial technique which relies on attention. Our model fuses teacher-side information and takes each layer's significance into consideration, then performs distillation between combined teacher layers and those of the student. Using our technique, we distilled a 12-layer BERT (Devlin et al. 2019) into 6-, 4-, and 2-layer counterparts and evaluated them on GLUE tasks (Wang et al. 2018). Experimental results show that our combinatorial approach is able to outperform other existing techniques.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Concise Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a logits-matching trick into a broad set of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from large neural teachers. Modern KD variants transfer soft predictions, intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational or contrastive structure; they are combined with data-centric practices (augmentation, synthetic and zero-shot data) and complementary compression (pruning, architecture search) to meet real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical work demonstrates strong gains in NLP (notably transformer compression) as well as vision, graphs, and federated settings, while theoretical and empirical studies reveal optimization challenges, teacher–student capacity mismatch, and distributional/heterogeneity limitations. Practical pipelines favor pretraining or progressive replacement, representation-level matching, task-adaptive data strategies, and awareness of privacy and robustness trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Feature-map-level Online Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Feature maps contain rich information about image intensity and spatial correlation. However, previous online knowledge distillation methods only utilize the class probabilities. Thus in this paper, we propose an online knowledge distillation method that transfers not only the knowledge of the class probabilities but also that of the feature map using the adversarial training framework. We train multiple networks simultaneously by employing discriminators to distinguish the feature map distributions of different networks. Each network has its corresponding discriminator which discriminates the feature map from its own as fake while classifying that of the other network as real. By training a network to fool the corresponding discriminator, it can learn the other network's feature map distribution. We show that our method performs better than the conventional direct alignment method such as L1 and is more suitable for online distillation. Also, we propose a novel cyclic learning scheme for training more than two networks together. We have applied our method to various network architectures on the classification task and discovered a significant improvement of performance especially in the case of training a pair of a small network and a large one.

papers_seen.author: Pham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical set of techniques to transfer predictive and representational knowledge from large, expensive teacher models to smaller, faster student models. Across computer vision, generative modeling, retrieval, and natural language processing, practitioners use KD to reduce inference cost, enable on-device deployment, and adapt models to new domains or privacy constraints. KD methods vary in what is transferred (soft targets, intermediate features, attention maps), how teacher and student are aligned (layer mapping, attention-weighted projection, task-aware filters), and whether original training data are available (data-free and zero-shot approaches). Success depends on careful choices of teacher preparation, student capacity and architecture, signal selection, and data or synthetic-sample strategies; when designed appropriately, KD combined with complementary compression (pruning, architecture transforms) yields compact models with strong empirical performance, while important limitations remain (representation mismatch, propagation of teacher biases, low-frequency token coverage).

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical and broadly applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster ones while retaining much of their performance. KD is effective across modalities and tasks, from question answering and speech recognition to vision and federated learning, but its success depends on careful handling of teacher imperfections, data artifacts, and deployment constraints. Best practices include using multi-teacher or staged distillation, blending soft and hard targets, engineering teacher-student interfaces (e.g., projectors or student-aware teachers), and combining KD with complementary techniques such as quantization or federated momentum. When these strategies are applied thoughtfully, KD enables high-quality compact models suitable for real-world, resource-constrained scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Adaptation: Teaching to Adapt
papers_seen.abstract: Domain adaptation is crucial in many real-world applications where the distribution of the training data differs from the distribution of the test data. Previous Deep Learning-based approaches to domain adaptation need to be trained jointly on source and target domain data and are therefore unappealing in scenarios where models need to be adapted to a large number of domains or where a domain is evolving, e.g. spam detection where attackers continuously change their tactics.   To fill this gap, we propose Knowledge Adaptation, an extension of Knowledge Distillation (Bucilua et al., 2006; Hinton et al., 2015) to the domain adaptation scenario. We show how a student model achieves state-of-the-art results on unsupervised domain adaptation from multiple sources on a standard sentiment analysis benchmark by taking into account the domain-specific expertise of multiple teachers and the similarities between their domains.   When learning from a single teacher, using domain similarity to gauge trustworthiness is inadequate. To this end, we propose a simple metric that correlates well with the teacher's accuracy in the target domain. We demonstrate that incorporating high-confidence examples selected by this metric enables the student model to achieve state-of-the-art performance in the single-source scenario.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Ball
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical but Nuanced Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach to compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones. When used thoughtfully, KD can preserve much of a teacher's performance while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. However, distillation is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on which signals are transferred (logits, features, relational information), alignment between teacher and student, availability or synthesis of suitable data, and awareness of teacher imperfections. Combining KD with representation-level matching, task-aware layer alignment, online or federated protocols, and data strategies yields the best trade-offs for real systems.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods have become central tools for deploying large deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. Work in this area spans techniques that transfer predictive behavior or internal representations from large teacher models to smaller students, approaches that operate without access to original training data, methods that preserve privacy or reduce communication in distributed settings, and specialized strategies for large pre-trained language and vision transformer models. Key themes include layer- and module-level mappings between teacher and student, task-aware selection of distilled signals, adversarial and generative approaches to synthesize training inputs, and the combination of pruning or architecture search with distillation. Practical trade-offs arise between fidelity to teacher behavior, student capacity, data availability, and robustness to distribution shifts or adversarial attacks. Ongoing challenges include aligning heterogeneous modalities and architectures, selecting what information to transfer for a given downstream task, and ensuring privacy and robustness while maintaining high compression ratios.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior or intermediate representations. Across modalities and tasks, distillation methods vary by what is transferred (logits/soft labels, intermediate features, attention, or structural knowledge), by whether they rely on original training data, and by how the teacher-student relationship is optimized. Practical goals include reducing inference cost, preserving accuracy under domain shift, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices, and improving robustness or fairness. Empirical work shows that carefully chosen transfer targets, training curricula, and data strategies can recover much of the teacher performance in compact models, and that meta-level and task-adaptive approaches further improve transfer effectiveness. Key open concerns are how to best align heterogeneous inputs or architectures, how to retain desirable inductive biases (e.g., for domain-specific tasks), and how to ensure reliable student performance without access to teacher training data.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Design-Sensitive Path to Compact Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation offers a practical route to compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of teacher performance. Its effectiveness arises from multiple distillation signals (soft labels, intermediate representations, attention or channel maps) and from combining distillation with pre-training, architecture-aware design, and data-management strategies. However, realizing these gains in real systems requires explicit choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited, private or heterogeneous data.

papers_seen.author: Mahoney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Not Universal Solution for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an effective and versatile strategy for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When carefully designed—choosing what to transfer (logits, features, relations), preparing or synthesizing appropriate data, and combining KD with complementary methods such as quantization or architecture search—distillation can produce compact models that retain much of teacher performance across modalities. However, KD has limits: teacher–student capacity mismatch, data heterogeneity or absence, and optimization subtleties can reduce gains. Practical deployment therefore benefits from hybrid pipelines that adapt KD objectives to task constraints, incorporate robustness and privacy considerations, and use auxiliary compression techniques where appropriate.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for creating smaller, faster models from larger ones while retaining much of their functionality. When combined with representation matching, architecture-aware surgery, selective sample strategies, and privacy-aware protocols, KD enables deployment of high-quality models across modalities and constrained environments. However, its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, and how to handle limited or sensitive data; without such care, distillation can underperform or transfer undesirable behaviors. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the central, composable tool in compression toolkits, and outlines concrete methodological priorities that practitioners should follow to realize reliable, efficient distilled models.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a single training trick into a flexible, task-aware toolkit for compressing large models into efficient students suitable for real-world deployment. KD can transfer output behavior, internal representations, and relational or structural knowledge; it can be adapted to constraints such as missing training data, privacy, distributed training, and domain shifts; and when combined with complementary techniques (architecture adaptation, pruning, task-aware layer selection) it produces compact models that retain much of the teacher's accuracy while meeting latency, memory, and privacy requirements. Practical use of KD requires matching the distillation strategy to the application constraints (what to transfer, which data to use, and how to align heterogeneous architectures).

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from large, often overparameterized teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while preserving performance. Across modalities and tasks, KD has evolved from simple soft-label matching to a diverse toolkit that includes intermediate representation matching, multi-teacher schedules, data-centric strategies (augmentation, data-free synthesis), online and distributed protocols, and task-aware adaptations. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how the student is initialized (including whether it is pre-trained), how the data distribution is shaped during distillation, and how robustness and rare-token behavior are addressed. Combining complementary techniques (pretraining, feature imitation, data mixing, and adaptive teacher strategies) produces compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints, but open issues remain around teacher selection, distributional mismatch, fairness, and adversarial robustness.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Online Knowledge Distillation via Mutual Contrastive Learning for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: The teacher-free online Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to train an ensemble of multiple student models collaboratively and distill knowledge from each other. Although existing online KD methods achieve desirable performance, they often focus on class probabilities as the core knowledge type, ignoring the valuable feature representational information. We present a Mutual Contrastive Learning (MCL) framework for online KD. The core idea of MCL is to perform mutual interaction and transfer of contrastive distributions among a cohort of networks in an online manner. Our MCL can aggregate cross-network embedding information and maximize the lower bound to the mutual information between two networks. This enables each network to learn extra contrastive knowledge from others, leading to better feature representations, thus improving the performance of visual recognition tasks. Beyond the final layer, we extend MCL to intermediate layers and perform an adaptive layer-matching mechanism trained by meta-optimization. Experiments on image classification and transfer learning to visual recognition tasks show that layer-wise MCL can lead to consistent performance gains against state-of-the-art online KD approaches. The superiority demonstrates that layer-wise MCL can guide the network to generate better feature representations. Our code is publicly avaliable at https://github.com/winycg/L-MCL.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques form a diverse toolkit for transferring information from larger, more expensive models to smaller, faster, or more constrained models. Methods range from matching output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, altering training curricula, and designing compression-aware teachers or architectures. These approaches have been applied across domains including vision, speech, translation, retrieval, and on-device deployment, and have been adapted to privacy- and communication-constrained settings. Empirical and analytical work has clarified different mechanisms by which distillation aids learning, and recent work explores automation, adversarial feature transfer, sample selection, and architecture-aware strategies to improve efficiency without sacrificing much performance.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Highlight Every Step: Knowledge Distillation via Collaborative Teaching
papers_seen.abstract: High storage and computational costs obstruct deep neural networks to be deployed on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation aims to train a compact student network by transferring knowledge from a larger pre-trained teacher model. However, most existing methods on knowledge distillation ignore the valuable information among training process associated with training results. In this paper, we provide a new Collaborative Teaching Knowledge Distillation (CTKD) strategy which employs two special teachers. Specifically, one teacher trained from scratch (i.e., scratch teacher) assists the student step by step using its temporary outputs. It forces the student to approach the optimal path towards the final logits with high accuracy. The other pre-trained teacher (i.e., expert teacher) guides the student to focus on a critical region which is more useful for the task. The combination of the knowledge from two special teachers can significantly improve the performance of the student network in knowledge distillation. The results of experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and Tiny ImageNet datasets verify that the proposed knowledge distillation method is efficient and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Contemporary Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural relationships. Across computer vision and natural language processing, a wide family of distillation strategies—ranging from soft-label (logit) matching to feature- and attention-level imitation, multi-teacher and online schemes, many-to-many layer mappings, and task-aware layer selection—has been developed to trade off accuracy, latency, and model size for practical deployment. Empirical work shows that combining distillation with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware transformations) and adapting distillation signals to task and data constraints yields compact models that capture much of teacher performance. At the same time, distillation must contend with capacity mismatch, robustness and distribution-shift sensitivity, privacy concerns, and the need for principled layer- and signal-alignment strategies—areas that motivate continued methodological and theoretical work.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression and Robust Deployment in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach to compressing large models into smaller, faster models while preserving— and in some settings improving—accuracy, robustness, and domain suitability. KD can be adapted to resource-constrained deployment, domain adaptation, privacy- or data-limited settings, and to improve adversarial robustness when paired with targeted techniques. Combining KD with complementary compression methods (e.g., pruning, structured sparsity, layer mapping) yields practical, high-quality compressed models across modalities including vision, language, graphs, and generative models.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core practical approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students while retaining much of the original performance. Multiple distillation mechanisms—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, adversarial/ensemble-based transfer, and data-free or selective-sample techniques—allow KD to address constraints such as limited data, heterogeneous deployment, low-precision hardware, and domain shift. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often acts both as a transfer of representational structure and as a regularizer; its success depends on choices about what is transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, how training data (real or synthetic) are used, and which complementary compression methods are applied. Remaining practical challenges include distributional mismatch, heterogeneity of architectures and devices, and principled teacher selection and optimization strategies.

papers_seen.author: Figueroa
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression strategies condense large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster, or lower-precision students suitable for deployment under resource, latency, and privacy constraints. Research has produced a taxonomy of approaches—soft-target (logit) supervision, intermediate/feature imitation, relational or attention-based losses, multi-teacher fusion, data-free and zero-shot protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work demonstrates that properly designed distillation pipelines can preserve most teacher performance across vision and language tasks while enabling substantial gains in inference speed and memory; theoretical analyses attribute much of KD’s benefit to regularization from soft targets and the transfer of inductive biases. Remaining challenges include handling teacher–student capacity mismatch, preserving robustness and fine-grained behaviors, operating without original training data, and designing adaptive, task-aware distillation signals.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques aim to transfer predictive behavior from large, expensive models to smaller, faster models so they can be deployed under resource, latency, or privacy constraints. Over the past decade research has produced a taxonomy of distillation mechanisms (logit/soft-target matching, representation or feature imitation, multi-teacher and ensemble-to-student transfers), adaptations for low-data or data-free settings, and combinations of distillation with architecture search and pruning. Empirical work shows that distilled students can recover much of teacher performance at large computational savings, but also highlights practical failure modes: students often do not perfectly match teacher predictive distributions, optimization choices and training data matter strongly, and specialized methods are needed for task-specific or distributed scenarios. Recent advances emphasize multi-stage/multi-teacher schedules, augmentation-aware objectives, online distributed training, and loss formulations that better capture teacher uncertainty; combining these approaches with automated architecture search and structured pruning yields stronger, hardware-aware compressed models.
