Combining richer teacher signals (intermediate representations, attention maps, or learned teacher updates), stronger input-side practices (data augmentation), and complementary compression methods (architecture search, pruning) yields robust, efficient students suitable for real-world constraints. This paper argues that distillation should be treated not as a single recipe but as a flexible toolkit whose components are chosen to match task constraints, and it highlights promising techniques to improve transfer fidelity, training efficiency, and downstream performance."}]

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Adversarial Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) has made remarkable progress in the last few years and become a popular paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer. However, almost all existing KD algorithms are data-driven, i.e., relying on a large amount of original training data or alternative data, which is usually unavailable in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we devote ourselves to this challenging problem and propose a novel adversarial distillation mechanism to craft a compact student model without any real-world data. We introduce a model discrepancy to quantificationally measure the difference between student and teacher models and construct an optimizable upper bound. In our work, the student and the teacher jointly act the role of the discriminator to reduce this discrepancy, when a generator adversarially produces some "hard samples" to enlarge it. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed data-free method yields comparable performance to existing data-driven methods. More strikingly, our approach can be directly extended to semantic segmentation, which is more complicated than classification, and our approach achieves state-of-the-art results. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/VainF/Data-Free-Adversarial-Distillation.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Concise Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a logits-matching trick into a broad set of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from large neural teachers. Modern KD variants transfer soft predictions, intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational or contrastive structure; they are combined with data-centric practices (augmentation, synthetic and zero-shot data) and complementary compression (pruning, architecture search) to meet real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical work demonstrates strong gains in NLP (notably transformer compression) as well as vision, graphs, and federated settings, while theoretical and empirical studies reveal optimization challenges, teacher–student capacity mismatch, and distributional/heterogeneity limitations. Practical pipelines favor pretraining or progressive replacement, representation-level matching, task-adaptive data strategies, and awareness of privacy and robustness trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Learning Student-Friendly Teacher Networks for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel knowledge distillation approach to facilitate the transfer of dark knowledge from a teacher to a student. Contrary to most of the existing methods that rely on effective training of student models given pretrained teachers, we aim to learn the teacher models that are friendly to students and, consequently, more appropriate for knowledge transfer. In other words, at the time of optimizing a teacher model, the proposed algorithm learns the student branches jointly to obtain student-friendly representations. Since the main goal of our approach lies in training teacher models and the subsequent knowledge distillation procedure is straightforward, most of the existing knowledge distillation methods can adopt this technique to improve the performance of diverse student models in terms of accuracy and convergence speed. The proposed algorithm demonstrates outstanding accuracy in several well-known knowledge distillation techniques with various combinations of teacher and student models even in the case that their architectures are heterogeneous and there is no prior knowledge about student models at the time of training teacher networks.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for creating smaller, faster models from larger ones while retaining much of their functionality. When combined with representation matching, architecture-aware surgery, selective sample strategies, and privacy-aware protocols, KD enables deployment of high-quality models across modalities and constrained environments. However, its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, and how to handle limited or sensitive data; without such care, distillation can underperform or transfer undesirable behaviors. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the central, composable tool in compression toolkits, and outlines concrete methodological priorities that practitioners should follow to realize reliable, efficient distilled models.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central strategy for compressing large neural networks into compact, deployable models across computer vision, generative modeling, and natural language processing. KD techniques extend beyond matching teacher output probabilities to include distillation of intermediate representations, layer-level mappings, and training without access to original data. Practical applications span compressing generative adversarial networks, pre-trained language models, and low-precision networks, while also addressing robustness and privacy constraints. Empirical work shows that carefully designed distillation protocols can retain most of a teacher's performance or even improve downstream robustness and inference efficiency, though success depends on choices such as what knowledge to transfer, architectural alignment, and availability of data or suitable synthetic surrogates.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques are widely used to transfer predictive behavior and representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. A broad family of methods—ranging from soft-target (logit) matching to feature- and layer-level mimicry, multi-teacher fusion, online and teacher-free protocols, and data-free or privacy-aware synthesis—has been developed and evaluated across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. Empirical studies show that, when designed carefully (teacher selection, data strategy, and objective choice), KD can preserve much of teacher performance while enabling practical deployment; however, limitations remain around domain shift, robustness, preservation of fine-grained behaviors, and data- or architecture-mismatch, motivating hybrid strategies that combine distillation with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware training.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring information from a teacher model. Across computer vision, language, graph, and healthcare applications, KD variants augment or replace naive logit matching with feature/hint matching, data augmentation, layer mapping strategies, and data-free or privacy-aware mechanisms. Practical work emphasizes task-adaptive compression, many-to-many layer alignment for pre-trained transformers, and the use of synthetic or mixed inputs to improve student generalization. At the same time, theoretical and empirical studies highlight limitations under data heterogeneity and imperfect teachers, motivating hybrid losses that mix soft and hard labels and methods that control privacy leakage during distillation.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Regularizing, and Flexible Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Beyond simple logit matching, KD encompasses transferring intermediate representations, relational structure, and ensemble behavior; it can be applied with or without access to original training data and can be combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet deployment constraints. KD often acts as an implicit regularizer that shapes the learning dynamics of students, and careful design of what to transfer and how—along with adaptations for data scarcity, privacy, and distributed settings—determines practical success. While KD is not a universal solution and depends on choices about teacher design, data, and alignment strategies, a hybrid, task-aware KD protocol enables high-quality compression across modalities and deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Online Knowledge Distillation via Mutual Contrastive Learning for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: The teacher-free online Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to train an ensemble of multiple student models collaboratively and distill knowledge from each other. Although existing online KD methods achieve desirable performance, they often focus on class probabilities as the core knowledge type, ignoring the valuable feature representational information. We present a Mutual Contrastive Learning (MCL) framework for online KD. The core idea of MCL is to perform mutual interaction and transfer of contrastive distributions among a cohort of networks in an online manner. Our MCL can aggregate cross-network embedding information and maximize the lower bound to the mutual information between two networks. This enables each network to learn extra contrastive knowledge from others, leading to better feature representations, thus improving the performance of visual recognition tasks. Beyond the final layer, we extend MCL to intermediate layers and perform an adaptive layer-matching mechanism trained by meta-optimization. Experiments on image classification and transfer learning to visual recognition tasks show that layer-wise MCL can lead to consistent performance gains against state-of-the-art online KD approaches. The superiority demonstrates that layer-wise MCL can guide the network to generate better feature representations. Our code is publicly avaliable at https://github.com/winycg/L-MCL.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Practical Prescriptions for Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, efficient students suitable for deployment. While KD reliably reduces model size and inference cost, its effectiveness depends critically on choices around teacher design, the training signal (soft labels vs. representations), the data used for distillation, and additional constraints such as fairness and privacy. To realize reliable, high-quality compressed models in NLP and related domains, practitioners should treat KD as a system composed of complementary ingredients—data augmentation, multi-teacher or meta-learned teachers, representation-level objectives, and interventions for bias and privacy—rather than a single off-the-shelf loss.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Compression and Robustness in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, multifaceted technique for compressing large models while often preserving — and sometimes improving — task performance. KD can transfer ensemble behaviour, provide regularization benefits, enable deployment under privacy or communication constraints, and be adapted to domain-specific and generation tasks. Practical KD implementations leverage ensembles, feature-level projectors, data augmentation, self-distillation, or data-free/federated protocols depending on resource and data availability. This paper argues that KD should be treated not only as a compression trick but as a general-purpose training paradigm with distinct theoretical and practical consequences for representation quality, robustness, and deployability.

papers_seen.author: Duncan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, faster models by transferring information from a teacher to a student. Techniques range from matching output distributions to transferring intermediate representations, feature maps, or distilled data. Applications span model compression for deployment (including transformer compression for NLP), multimodal model adaptation, federated and resource-constrained learning, and improving robustness or fairness. Practical strategies include layer-wise or attention-based projection, progressive module replacement, adversarial and data-free distillation, and task-specific adaptations that account for data heterogeneity and inductive bias.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression methods form a diverse toolkit for producing smaller, faster, or more deployable models while retaining much of the performance of larger teachers. Research spans soft-label and self-distillation strategies, layer- and representation-level transfers, architecture-aware and task-adaptive compression, and deployment-aware approaches that combine pruning, quantization, and distillation. Empirical work shows that careful choice of distillation signal (logits, intermediate representations, or feature maps), alignment strategy between teacher and student layers, data augmentation, and optimization scheduling materially affects student performance. Practical systems exploit these design choices to compress large pre-trained language models, accelerate inference, enable heterogeneous-device training, or improve low-precision networks. Despite progress, open questions remain about principled objective design, sample efficiency under limited data, and theory connecting transferred representations to generalization.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other learned structure. Methods span data-dependent distillation using teacher soft targets and intermediate hints, multi-teacher and ensemble compression, many-to-many layer mapping for large pre-trained language models, data-free or zero-shot distillation where training data are unavailable, and approaches that combine distillation with quantization or pruning for deployment. Empirical results demonstrate that distillation can recover much of a teacher's accuracy while enabling efficiency gains, but trade-offs remain around robustness, optimization difficulty, domain shifts, and the need for careful alignment of inputs or representations. Recent work addresses these challenges with generative replay, adversarial objectives, layer-matching distances, and teacher-annealing strategies, yet open problems include theory of optimization, scalable privacy-preserving protocols, and balancing fairness or robustness with compression.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: MEAL: Multi-Model Ensemble via Adversarial Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Often the best performing deep neural models are ensembles of multiple base-level networks. Unfortunately, the space required to store these many networks, and the time required to execute them at test-time, prohibits their use in applications where test sets are large (e.g., ImageNet). In this paper, we present a method for compressing large, complex trained ensembles into a single network, where knowledge from a variety of trained deep neural networks (DNNs) is distilled and transferred to a single DNN. In order to distill diverse knowledge from different trained (teacher) models, we propose to use adversarial-based learning strategy where we define a block-wise training loss to guide and optimize the predefined student network to recover the knowledge in teacher models, and to promote the discriminator network to distinguish teacher vs. student features simultaneously. The proposed ensemble method (MEAL) of transferring distilled knowledge with adversarial learning exhibits three important advantages: (1) the student network that learns the distilled knowledge with discriminators is optimized better than the original model; (2) fast inference is realized by a single forward pass, while the performance is even better than traditional ensembles from multi-original models; (3) the student network can learn the distilled knowledge from a teacher model that has arbitrary structures. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100, SVHN and ImageNet datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our MEAL method. On ImageNet, our ResNet-50 based MEAL achieves top-1/5 21.79%/5.99% val error, which outperforms the original model by 2.06%/1.14%. Code and models are available at: https://github.com/AaronHeee/MEAL

papers_seen.author: Hamilton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Core for Model Compression with Clear Limits and Research Priorities
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones across vision, speech, and language. KD combines multiple signals (soft-labels, intermediate representations, attention and feature matching, synthetic-data generation) and integrates naturally with complementary compression methods. However, its practical success depends on careful teacher–student design, access to appropriate data (or robust data-free methods), and mitigation of optimization, robustness, and fairness risks. This paper argues that KD should remain central to compression pipelines while research focuses on principled teacher selection, reliable data-free distillation, representation-aware objectives, and safeguards for privacy and bias.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Tool for Practical Model Compression across Modalities
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic for transferring soft logits to a rich family of techniques that enable deployment of large models in resource-constrained settings. Across NLP, vision, generative modeling, and cross-modal systems, distillation methods that match intermediate representations, adapt teacher signals to student inputs, exploit many-to-many layer correspondences, and combine with pruning or ensemble guidance consistently produce compact models with near-teacher performance. KD is also effective for domain adaptation and continual learning, making it a practical foundation for producing small, fast, and robust models for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: The Case for Practical, Adaptive Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible tool for compressing large deep learning models into deployable students. Recent work shows KD can both directly reduce model size and serve as a mechanism to transfer inductive biases, intermediate representations, and task-specific attention. However, real-world constraints — limited or private training data, domain and client heterogeneity, and redundant teacher representations — require KD methods that are data-free, adversarially robust, task-aware, and selective about what teacher knowledge to transfer.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: ALP-KD: Attention-Based Layer Projection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is considered as a training and compression strategy in which two neural networks, namely a teacher and a student, are coupled together during training. The teacher network is supposed to be a trustworthy predictor and the student tries to mimic its predictions. Usually, a student with a lighter architecture is selected so we can achieve compression and yet deliver high-quality results. In such a setting, distillation only happens for final predictions whereas the student could also benefit from teacher's supervision for internal components.   Motivated by this, we studied the problem of distillation for intermediate layers. Since there might not be a one-to-one alignment between student and teacher layers, existing techniques skip some teacher layers and only distill from a subset of them. This shortcoming directly impacts quality, so we instead propose a combinatorial technique which relies on attention. Our model fuses teacher-side information and takes each layer's significance into consideration, then performs distillation between combined teacher layers and those of the student. Using our technique, we distilled a 12-layer BERT (Devlin et al. 2019) into 6-, 4-, and 2-layer counterparts and evaluated them on GLUE tasks (Wang et al. 2018). Experimental results show that our combinatorial approach is able to outperform other existing techniques.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structured relationships. Across deep learning and NLP, KD enables deployment of performant models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints and is routinely combined with complementary compression methods. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer (logits vs. features), how to align teacher and student architectures, the availability and design of distillation data (real, augmented, or synthetic), and training protocols that mitigate capacity and distribution mismatches. Open challenges include robust teacher selection, data- and domain-mismatch, and scaling distillation methods to heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive deployments.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques enable deploying large pretrained models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations from high-capacity teachers to smaller students. Methods include transferring softened output distributions, matching intermediate features or attention maps, layer- and task-aware alignment, online and mutual distillation, and data-free approaches that synthesize surrogate inputs. Empirical evidence across vision and language tasks shows that well-designed distillation can preserve most teacher performance while substantially reducing model size, latency, and energy use. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to map heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle limited or private data. Remaining challenges center on preserving low-frequency or rare-token behavior in sequence models, avoiding transfer of biases or adversarial vulnerabilities, and jointly optimizing compression for hardware and task constraints.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural knowledge. Methods span matching softened output distributions, feature- and attention-level imitation, layer mapping and progressive module replacement, channel- and module-aware transfers, and data-free or generative approaches for when original training data are unavailable. Practical pipelines combine KD with quantization, low-precision training, pruning, or architecture transformations and often rely on staged or adaptive teacher-student schedules. Empirical evidence shows KD can yield compact models that retain much of teacher performance across vision and NLP tasks, but success depends on teacher quality, what and which samples are distilled, data availability, and careful engineering of interfaces between heterogeneous teacher and student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Powers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Compressing and Adapting Deep Models in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster students while preserving or even improving task performance. Across settings—domain adaptation, resource-constrained deployment, privacy-limited releases, sequence generation, and large-scale distributed training—distillation methods enable trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and cost. By leveraging teacher signals (soft targets, feature representations, or ensembles), self-distillation, and data- or communication-efficient protocols, practitioners can tailor compression strategies to meet production constraints without wholesale redesign of model architectures.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: VPN++: Rethinking Video-Pose embeddings for understanding Activities of Daily Living
papers_seen.abstract: Many attempts have been made towards combining RGB and 3D poses for the recognition of Activities of Daily Living (ADL). ADL may look very similar and often necessitate to model fine-grained details to distinguish them. Because the recent 3D ConvNets are too rigid to capture the subtle visual patterns across an action, this research direction is dominated by methods combining RGB and 3D Poses. But the cost of computing 3D poses from RGB stream is high in the absence of appropriate sensors. This limits the usage of aforementioned approaches in real-world applications requiring low latency. Then, how to best take advantage of 3D Poses for recognizing ADL? To this end, we propose an extension of a pose driven attention mechanism: Video-Pose Network (VPN), exploring two distinct directions. One is to transfer the Pose knowledge into RGB through a feature-level distillation and the other towards mimicking pose driven attention through an attention-level distillation. Finally, these two approaches are integrated into a single model, we call VPN++. We show that VPN++ is not only effective but also provides a high speed up and high resilience to noisy Poses. VPN++, with or without 3D Poses, outperforms the representative baselines on 4 public datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/srijandas07/vpnplusplus.

papers_seen.author: Cruz
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable paradigm for transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller, more efficient students. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, KD methods—ranging from matching teacher output distributions to aligning intermediate representations and relational structure—enable substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to obtain or synthesize training data, and whether to complement distillation with adversarial or ensemble signals. When these elements are chosen and tuned for task and deployment constraints, KD produces compact models that are effective in resource-limited and application-specific settings.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Flexible Core Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not a single recipe but a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large models into compact students suitable for deployment. When combined with task-aware architecture choices, ensemble or self-generated signals, and orthogonal compression methods, KD reliably reduces inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Careful attention to what is distilled, data strategy, and training dynamics mitigates common failure modes and enables robust, real-world compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses larger models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and intermediate representations. Across vision, speech, and language tasks KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while often preserving most of the teacher’s performance. Practical use of KD involves choices about what to transfer (logits, features, attention), how to handle data mismatches (data augmentation, synthetic data, or data-free methods), and how to combine distillation with complementary techniques (pretraining, pruning, quantization, federated protocols). Despite broad empirical success, open problems remain in preserving low-frequency behaviors, robustness and fairness, and in designing principled curricula and teacher-student interfaces for diverse deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression strategies have become central tools to deploy large deep models in resource-constrained settings. The literature shows diverse KD objectives (soft-label matching, representation matching, relational/correlation losses), architectural strategies (layer-wise, task-adaptive, student-friendly teacher training), data approaches (data augmentation, distilled or synthesized surrogates, zero-shot), and multi-teacher or ensemble-to-single compression. Empirical work across vision, generative models, reinforcement learning, and language tasks (including BERT compression and non-autoregressive translation) reveals consistent trade-offs between compression, accuracy, and robustness, and highlights practical constraints such as data heterogeneity and teacher-student capacity mismatch. Below we synthesize methods, observed benefits, limitations, and practical recommendations grounded in the provided literature.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: The Central Role and Practical Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a core set of techniques for converting large, expensive neural models into smaller, faster students suitable for real-world deployment. KD variants transfer soft outputs, intermediate representations, or structural behaviors; they can be combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture modification) and adapted for constrained data, privacy, and deployment regimes. However, distillation’s success depends on principled choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, how to obtain or synthesize training data, and how to mitigate teacher-induced errors or biases. Practical deployments therefore require task-aware distillation design, careful teacher selection or adaptation, and evaluation of failure modes such as degraded rare-token behavior or domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Keith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, Applications, and Limitations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and richer internal signals. Techniques extend beyond matching teacher logits to include feature- and attention-level imitation, relational objectives, adversarially-generated or adversarially-robust signals, online and multi-teacher schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware variants. These methods enable deployment of compact models across vision and NLP tasks (including compressing pretrained transformers), improve efficiency on-device, and can sometimes preserve or even enhance robustness and generalization. Success depends on choices of distillation target, student architecture and capacity, the nature and availability of distillation data, and handling of domain or agent heterogeneity; open issues include transferring robustness reliably, avoiding propagation of teacher biases, and principled handling of heterogeneous or private data sources.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: Selective Knowledge Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Neural Machine Translation (NMT) models achieve state-of-the-art performance on many translation benchmarks. As an active research field in NMT, knowledge distillation is widely applied to enhance the model's performance by transferring teacher model's knowledge on each training sample. However, previous work rarely discusses the different impacts and connections among these samples, which serve as the medium for transferring teacher knowledge. In this paper, we design a novel protocol that can effectively analyze the different impacts of samples by comparing various samples' partitions. Based on above protocol, we conduct extensive experiments and find that the teacher's knowledge is not the more, the better. Knowledge over specific samples may even hurt the whole performance of knowledge distillation. Finally, to address these issues, we propose two simple yet effective strategies, i.e., batch-level and global-level selections, to pick suitable samples for distillation. We evaluate our approaches on two large-scale machine translation tasks, WMT'14 English->German and WMT'19 Chinese->English. Experimental results show that our approaches yield up to +1.28 and +0.89 BLEU points improvements over the Transformer baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Russell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer information from large teacher models to smaller students to enable deployment under resource, latency, or privacy constraints. Methods extend beyond matching teacher logits to include feature- and attention-level transfer, multi-teacher and staged pipelines, data- and augmentation-aware protocols, and combinations with low-precision or architecture-aware compression. Empirical results across vision, language, graph, and generation tasks show that careful selection of what to transfer, how to prepare students, and how to handle data mismatches determines the practical trade-offs between model size, speed, and retained performance. Open problems include robustness under data scarcity, heterogeneous architecture alignment, and preserving rare-token or domain-specific behaviors during compression.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural knowledge. Methods span matching softened output distributions, feature- and attention-level imitation, layer mapping and progressive module replacement, channel- and module-aware transfers, and data-free or generative approaches for when original training data are unavailable. Practical pipelines combine KD with quantization, low-precision training, pruning, or architecture transformations and often rely on staged or adaptive teacher-student schedules. Empirical evidence shows KD can yield compact models that retain much of teacher performance across vision and NLP tasks, but success depends on teacher quality, what and which samples are distilled, data availability, and careful engineering of interfaces between heterogeneous teacher and student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Whitehead
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Strategy for Practical Model Compression: Strengths, Mechanisms, and Remaining Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a proven, flexible strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision and NLP. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while enabling large reductions in parameters and latency, and it generalizes across settings from data-poor or privacy-sensitive deployments to multi-teacher and online training regimes. However, practical success depends on careful choice of what to transfer (logits, features, relations), handling limited or absent training data, mitigating transferred biases, and aligning teacher-student architectures. I argue that KD should be the primary tool in production compression pipelines but must be combined with data synthesis, teacher selection/calibration, and fairness-aware design to realize robust, reliable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment. Research over the past decade has produced a wide array of distillation variants (logit-based supervision, feature and attention matching, multi- and self-distillation, data-free methods) and shown how KD can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet practical constraints. Empirical and theoretical work identifies both the strengths of KD (regularization, practical deployment gains, domain adaptation) and its limits (optimization difficulty, capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors), motivating a pragmatic set of design choices for robust compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Adapt-and-Distill: Developing Small, Fast and Effective Pretrained Language Models for Domains
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have achieved great success in many natural language processing tasks. However, when they are applied in specific domains, these models suffer from domain shift and bring challenges in fine-tuning and online serving for latency and capacity constraints. In this paper, we present a general approach to developing small, fast and effective pre-trained models for specific domains. This is achieved by adapting the off-the-shelf general pre-trained models and performing task-agnostic knowledge distillation in target domains. Specifically, we propose domain-specific vocabulary expansion in the adaptation stage and employ corpus level occurrence probability to choose the size of incremental vocabulary automatically. Then we systematically explore different strategies to compress the large pre-trained models for specific domains. We conduct our experiments in the biomedical and computer science domain. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves better performance over the BERT BASE model in domain-specific tasks while 3.3x smaller and 5.1x faster than BERT BASE. The code and pre-trained models are available at https://aka.ms/adalm.

papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a System: Practical Strengths, Limits, and Prescriptions for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a modular system—combining soft-target supervision, representation-level objectives, data augmentation, multi-teacher signals, and complementary compression methods—KD reliably yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance across vision, language, graph, and generative tasks. Effectiveness depends on handling data availability, architecture mismatches, and undesirable teacher artifacts; these constraints are manageable when KD is designed with domain adaptation, input alignment, and augmentation-aware strategies. I argue KD should be the default toolchain for producing production-ready compact models, applied with explicit attention to what knowledge is transferred and how it is matched to student capacity and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile model-compression paradigm that transfers predictive behavior from larger (teacher) models to smaller (student) models. Work across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks has expanded KD beyond soft-label matching to include internal representation matching, layer mapping, feature attention, curriculum strategies, data-side techniques (including data-free methods and augmentation-aware KD), multi-teacher weighting, and task-specific adaptations. Empirical and theoretical analyses show that KD can act both as a conduit of teacher “dark knowledge” (similarity structure among classes) and as a regularizer related to label smoothing; practical improvements require matching the right kinds of knowledge (outputs, intermediate features, relational signals) and addressing mismatches in inputs, data distributions, and training curricula. Applications in NLP (e.g., retrieval, translation, spoken QA) illustrate how KD strategies must be adapted to task structure and data idiosyncrasies to preserve quality on low-frequency phenomena while achieving significant runtime and memory savings.

papers_seen.author: Holmes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches and Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of their performance. Work across NLP and broader deep learning has developed multiple KD paradigms—soft-label (logit) matching, intermediate-representation matching, layer-to-layer and many-to-many layer mapping, multi-teacher aggregation, and data-free distillation—and combined KD with other compression methods such as quantization, pruning, and architecture search. Empirical results show that well-designed distillation can yield compact models that approach the accuracy of large pre-trained models while offering substantial savings in parameters, latency, and computational cost. Remaining challenges include aligning heterogeneous teacher and student architectures, coping with limited or unavailable training data, and selecting or weighting multiple teachers per example. The literature suggests principled strategies—attention-based layer fusion, representation-level losses, teacher confidence or dynamic weighting, and synthetic-data generation—that mitigate these issues and enable effective deployment of compressed models in domain-specific and resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for creating smaller, faster models from larger ones while retaining much of their functionality. When combined with representation matching, architecture-aware surgery, selective sample strategies, and privacy-aware protocols, KD enables deployment of high-quality models across modalities and constrained environments. However, its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, and how to handle limited or sensitive data; without such care, distillation can underperform or transfer undesirable behaviors. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the central, composable tool in compression toolkits, and outlines concrete methodological priorities that practitioners should follow to realize reliable, efficient distilled models.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not a mere optimization trick but a central, versatile toolkit for compressing large models into compact, deployable students. When treated as a system composed of complementary ingredients—teacher design (single, ensemble or multi-teacher), what to transfer (logits, intermediate representations, relational information), how to obtain data (real, synthesized, or data-free), and deployment constraints (privacy, federated or on-device latency)—KD consistently enables strong trade-offs between efficiency and performance across vision, language, generative, and real-world production tasks. Realizing KD’s full potential requires representation- and layer-aware objectives, adaptive teacher–student mappings, careful handling of data scarcity or privacy, and integration with pretraining and other compression methods.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is the most pragmatic and versatile route to make large deep models usable in constrained settings. When treated as a flexible toolkit—not merely as soft-label matching—KD enables compact models that preserve student performance, transfer intermediate representations, and support deployment constraints such as limited data, heterogeneous devices, or low-precision inference. Real-world success requires combining KD with task-aware layer mapping, multi-teacher or ensemble signals, data-generation or adversarial synthesis when original data are unavailable, and joint use with quantization or precision-reduction. These combinations produce students that are both efficient and robust enough for production use.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Compression and Transfer in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured beyond a single recipe for copying soft labels: it is a flexible set of techniques that address model compression, domain and task transfer, privacy-constrained scenarios, distributed training, and continual learning. Practical KD variants operate at different levels (logits, features, layers), use data augmentation or synthetic data when real data are unavailable, and adapt training schedules to the target application. When chosen to match the constraints of the deployment setting—data availability, compute budget, task type, and model architecture—KD consistently enables smaller or more specialized students to approach or sometimes exceed teacher performance while offering operational benefits such as faster inference, lower memory, and more reproducible training.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Concise Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a logits-matching trick into a broad set of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from large neural teachers. Modern KD variants transfer soft predictions, intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational or contrastive structure; they are combined with data-centric practices (augmentation, synthetic and zero-shot data) and complementary compression (pruning, architecture search) to meet real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical work demonstrates strong gains in NLP (notably transformer compression) as well as vision, graphs, and federated settings, while theoretical and empirical studies reveal optimization challenges, teacher–student capacity mismatch, and distributional/heterogeneity limitations. Practical pipelines favor pretraining or progressive replacement, representation-level matching, task-adaptive data strategies, and awareness of privacy and robustness trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: No One Left Behind: Inclusive Federated Learning over Heterogeneous Devices
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is an important paradigm for training global models from decentralized data in a privacy-preserving way. Existing FL methods usually assume the global model can be trained on any participating client. However, in real applications, the devices of clients are usually heterogeneous, and have different computing power. Although big models like BERT have achieved huge success in AI, it is difficult to apply them to heterogeneous FL with weak clients. The straightforward solutions like removing the weak clients or using a small model to fit all clients will lead to some problems, such as under-representation of dropped clients and inferior accuracy due to data loss or limited model representation ability. In this work, we propose InclusiveFL, a client-inclusive federated learning method to handle this problem. The core idea of InclusiveFL is to assign models of different sizes to clients with different computing capabilities, bigger models for powerful clients and smaller ones for weak clients. We also propose an effective method to share the knowledge among multiple local models with different sizes. In this way, all the clients can participate in the model learning in FL, and the final model can be big and powerful enough. Besides, we propose a momentum knowledge distillation method to better transfer knowledge in big models on powerful clients to the small models on weak clients. Extensive experiments on many real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in learning accurate models from clients with heterogeneous devices under the FL framework.

papers_seen.author: Cobb
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models by transferring information from one or more high-capacity teachers to a smaller student model. The field has evolved from simple soft-label matching to rich objectives that align intermediate representations, exploit multiple teachers, search for task-specific student architectures, and generate or synthesize data when original training sets are unavailable. Distillation is applied across modalities (language, speech, vision, graphs) and combined with other compression techniques to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical and theoretical work highlights both practical gains and recurring challenges — data availability, teacher–student heterogeneity, preserving rare or domain-specific behaviors, and principled objective design — and suggests strategies to mitigate them in deployed systems.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior or intermediate representations. Across modalities and tasks, distillation methods vary by what is transferred (logits/soft labels, intermediate features, attention, or structural knowledge), by whether they rely on original training data, and by how the teacher-student relationship is optimized. Practical goals include reducing inference cost, preserving accuracy under domain shift, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices, and improving robustness or fairness. Empirical work shows that carefully chosen transfer targets, training curricula, and data strategies can recover much of the teacher performance in compact models, and that meta-level and task-adaptive approaches further improve transfer effectiveness. Key open concerns are how to best align heterogeneous inputs or architectures, how to retain desirable inductive biases (e.g., for domain-specific tasks), and how to ensure reliable student performance without access to teacher training data.

papers_seen.author: Rasmussen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Compressing Deep Models in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach that enables deploying high-performing deep models by transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller students. KD operates through multiple mechanisms—matching soft outputs, imitating intermediate representations, and shaping relational structure—and can be combined with pre-training, architecture search, low-precision numerics, and data synthesis to meet real deployment constraints. When chosen and applied carefully (appropriate targets, student pre-training, layer mappings, and consideration of data/privacy/ethical constraints), KD yields compact models that retain much of teacher accuracy while being suitable for latency-, memory-, or privacy-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques compress large neural models into smaller, faster, or more private students by transferring information from a teacher. Research over the past decade has explored a spectrum of KD variants — from soft-label logits transfer to feature-map matching, adversarial and online schemes, few-shot and privacy-preserving compression, and theoretical analyses of when and why distillation helps. Empirical work shows KD improves deployment practicality across vision, speech, NLP, graph, and generative models, while recent studies examine robustness, data-efficiency, the role of pre-training, and the impact of teacher quality. Important open directions include principled methods for sample selection, cross-domain transfer, formal guarantees under limited data or adversaries, and integrating KD with compression primitives such as pruning and structured sparsity.

papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Multifaceted Strategy for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep and NLP models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Beyond matching final outputs, modern KD variants transfer intermediate representations, adapt teacher behavior to students, and operate when task data are limited or unavailable. KD is most effective when combined with task-aware signal selection, teacher design, data strategies, and complementary compression such as architecture search or pruning; used in this way, KD enables compact models that approach teacher performance while addressing real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical and broadly applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster ones while retaining much of their performance. KD is effective across modalities and tasks, from question answering and speech recognition to vision and federated learning, but its success depends on careful handling of teacher imperfections, data artifacts, and deployment constraints. Best practices include using multi-teacher or staged distillation, blending soft and hard targets, engineering teacher-student interfaces (e.g., projectors or student-aware teachers), and combining KD with complementary techniques such as quantization or federated momentum. When these strategies are applied thoughtfully, KD enables high-quality compact models suitable for real-world, resource-constrained scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable ones by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural relations. Across vision and natural language tasks, KD variants—logits/soft-label matching, feature- and relation-level imitation, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols—enable substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while often retaining most of the teacher’s performance. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to generate or curate data for transfer, and how to align teacher and student capacity; common extensions address fairness, federated or distributed settings, and privacy constraints. Remaining challenges include optimization difficulties, propagation of teacher errors (especially on low-frequency phenomena), domain and device heterogeneity, and preserving robustness under distributional shift.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Compressing Deep and NLP Models: Methods, Limits, and Complementary Techniques
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a core strategy to compress large pre-trained deep models so they can be deployed in latency- and resource-constrained settings. KD variants—multi-teacher pipelines, layer-wise and task-aware alignment, self-distillation, and feature-level matching—enable small students to approach or match teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost. KD is most effective when combined with complementary approaches such as pruning and architecture search, and when adapted to domain or system constraints (e.g., federated or multi-device settings). However, KD is not a universal panacea: data heterogeneity, misaligned inputs between teacher and student, and inappropriate augmentation or feature transfer can limit gains, so careful design choices are required to realize practical compression.
